name: Tymnas
title: The Groundskeeper Who Lost Track of Time
status: Active — cottage damaged during vampire siege; current role in the reported outside ambush remains unclear
summary: Tymnas is an old satyr who has been tending the grounds of the Shadow Estate for long enough that he has stopped distinguishing between yesterday and last week. He has heavy black horns, dark weary eyes, grey hair still threaded with black, and an ash-grey fur cloak over leather binding that suggests someone who spends most of his time outdoors in a dimension that is not kind to outdoor living. He gave Markop Archie's watch — not knowing or not remembering when he had found it, casually remarking that he had 'seen Archie at the dinner tonight' when Markop noted that dinner was yesterday. He maintains a cottage in the hedge maze that is warmer and more colorful than anything else in the Shadow Estate, including rooms that cost considerably more to occupy. He knows where the tools shed is. He has directions to the grove. He does not know about the monsters in the grove because he stopped checking. Waluigi finds Tymnas deeply sympathetic — he is the kind of person who tends to beautiful things in a dimension that has no use for beauty, and has done so for long enough that the dimension's indifference no longer bothers him. WAH.
description:
Waluigi is documenting Tymnas because Tymnas is both a minor figure and a significant one, in the way that all groundskeepers at important locations are minor figures who know exactly where everything is.

## The Cottage — Color in a Colorless Place

Tymnas's cottage in the hedge maze is the Shadow Estate's most anomalous feature. Other rooms in the manor have color suppressed — everything drained toward grey and black by the Shadowfell's fundamental character. Tymnas's cottage is warm yellows and greens that 'practically strain against whatever force sucks the color from this plane, leaving them to glimmer richly at times.'

This resistance to the Shadowfell's bleaching is not explained. It could be Tymnas's age — a being old enough might have accumulated enough of something that keeps color alive. It could be the cottage's location within the maze, sheltered from the estate's more direct supernatural influence. It could be deliberate maintenance on Tymnas's part, the kind of quiet daily work that produces results nobody thinks to ask about.

The cottage has food that 'looks almost normal.' In a dimension where plants grow as colored-wrong reflections of material-plane originals, Tymnas has a table of recognizable produce. This is either magic or the most impressive gardening in the Shadowfell.

## Archie's Watch — What He Knew and When

Tymnas had Archie Miser's watch. He produced it for Markop — fiddling with it, then handing it over when the party asked.

The watch had Archie's initials. When Markop asked if Tymnas knew Archie Miser, Tymnas said he had seen Archie at the dinner tonight.

Markop noted that dinner was yesterday.

Tymnas said 'oh was it, sorry, lost track of time.'

This could be ordinary Shadowfell temporal disorientation — time flows sluggishly in this plane, and an entity who has lived here long enough might genuinely struggle to distinguish recent events from slightly less recent ones. It could also be something else. Tymnas had Archie's watch. He does not explain how he acquired it. He gives it away without apparent concern.

Waluigi notes: Archie's watch was among the items stolen by Mystic Morel during the song-and-robbery scene. If Tymnas had the watch after Morel took it, either Tymnas and Morel are connected, or the watch changed hands between the theft and Tymnas's possession through means neither has explained, or Tymnas had the watch before the robbery, which would mean Archie had already lost it once and it had been recovered and then stolen again.

Waluigi cannot resolve this. Waluigi is filing it under 'timeline inconsistency with possible significance.'

## The Grove Warning — What He Did Not Mention

Tymnas offered to let the party go to the grove. When Markop asked if there was anything dangerous there, Tymnas said thorns and bees. When Markop asked if there was anything else, Tymnas went into his room and came back with a trowel.

The grove contained Mazebounds. The grove contained a massive skull-faced tree with hanging corpses and shadow crows with crimson eyes. The grove was controlled by a hostile entity who sang at people and tried to drag them into eternal dance.

Tymnas mentioned thorns and bees.

Waluigi does not know whether Tymnas genuinely did not know about the Mazebounds or whether he knew and considered them not worth mentioning. Both possibilities are disturbing in different ways. A groundskeeper who doesn't know what's in the grounds he tends has been failing to check for some time. A groundskeeper who knows and doesn't say is making a choice about what information to share.

The trowel he retrieved was magical — Markop detected it. A magical trowel handed to visitors right before they walk into a dangerous grove. Waluigi is not saying Tymnas set them up. Waluigi is noting that every detail of this interaction can be read innocently or not innocently, and Waluigi has been in the Shadow Estate long enough  through accounts, not personally — to know that 'innocently' is the more dangerous assumption.

## Assessment

Tymnas is either a very old, slightly confused satyr who tends gardens in a death dimension because he has done so for too long to stop, or he is a subtle intelligence asset embedded in the estate's most frequently traversed non-building space, positioned to observe and occasionally redirect visitors.

Waluigi hopes he is the former. Waluigi suspects the latter is at least partially true.

The color in his cottage — the warmth, the food, the richness that resists the Shadowfell — suggests either unusual capability or unusual protection. Neither belongs to a simple groundskeeper.

And he had Archie's watch.

WAH.

## Latest Filing — 4 Aethel, 1040 BF

Tymnas's cottage suffered another lockdown: damaged hinges, a shattered window, an imp hidden in the broom closet, and a vampire admitted through the imp's invitation. Tymnas's own location during the confrontation is not established in the received account.

faiths.note: Tymnas has tended the Shadow Estate's grounds long enough to stop asking who owns them. The Circle's teaching that rot is a stage rather than a failure is, for a satyr gardening in the Shadowfell, simply the observed behaviour of the soil.

name: Bryan
title: The Toad God's Instrument of Judgment, Currently Lost in the Shadowfell
status: Active — last confirmed location: the Shadowfell grove, where a massive fireball was hurled at Mazebounds
affiliation: Servant of the Toad God / Affiliated with Mystic Morel's hunting party
summary: Bryan is the servant of a deity he calls the Toad God, and he arrived at Raventree's extended crisis with the mission-oriented certainty of someone who has received divine instruction and the practical limitations of someone who has never actually been to the Shadowfell. He recruited Dan from the Mages' Guild barracks, partnered with Mystic Morel for planar transit, and entered the Shadowfell hunting Archie Miser under a theological mandate that he described as being 'for the good of the world.' He found the Mazehound grove instead. A massive fireball was hurled. Waluigi does not know whose fireball it was or whether Bryan survived the grove encounter. Waluigi notes that anyone hunting Archie Miser in the Shadowfell while carrying a mandate from a Toad God and traveling with a fortune-telling pickpocket is operating at a significant information disadvantage relative to the situation they have entered. WAH.
description:
Waluigi is documenting Bryan because Bryan represents a threat category the party has not fully accounted for: the true believer.

## The Toad God — What Bryan Believes

Bryan serves a deity he identifies as the Toad God. Waluigi does not have extensive documentation on this entity — the Mushroom Kingdom's religious landscape is complex, and Toad deities range from minor nature spirits to genuine cosmic forces depending on which tradition you consult.

What Waluigi can determine from Bryan's behavior: the Toad God's mandate in this situation involves Archie Miser. Bryan believes Archie must be found. He recruited assistance, traveled across planes, and pursued leads through a dangerous Shadowfell grove based on this belief. He calls the hunt something done 'for the good of the world' — not for personal revenge, not for factional advantage, but for a moral purpose he receives from a divine source.

This makes Bryan different from the other parties hunting Archie. Mystic Morel has opaque personal motives. Dan's claimed revenge motivation appeared to be a lie — his actual commitment to the hunt was uncertain. But Bryan believes. That belief will not be talked out of him, cannot be bribed away, and does not diminish when things go badly.

Waluigi finds true believers more alarming than mercenaries. Mercenaries stop when the pay runs out. True believers stop when they are stopped.

## The Mages' Guild Barracks — Recruitment

Bryan entered the Mages' Guild barracks while Dan was sleeping and recruited him for the hunt.

The purple toad — Mystic Morel — had already been in Dan's room, had stolen a photograph from under his pillow showing the Vigilance crew including Archie, and had handed it to Bryan as intelligence. Bryan grabbed Morel by the torso when he saw Archie in the photograph, demanding immediate location information. Morel said Archie was at Raventree. Bryan said 'got it' and immediately began planning.

Bryan woke Dan, introduced himself as a servant of the Toad God, and asked whether Dan wanted revenge on Archie. Dan said yes — this appeared to be a lie, the zone-of-truth assessment later confirmed Dan's motives were not what he stated — but Bryan accepted the answer.

The recruitment scene tells Waluigi something about Bryan: he asks questions, accepts answers, and moves forward. He is not a sophisticated interrogator. He is a man with a mission who needs bodies and takes the available ones without extensive vetting.

## The Badge Removal — Morel's Operational Move

Before the hunting party transited to the Shadowfell, Mystic Morel removed the Mages' Guild tracking badges from Dan and the other mages present.

'By removing these tracking devices, we can go after Dan without the other members being involved,' Morel explained.

Bryan's response to this operational preparation suggests he either trusted Morel completely or was focused enough on the mission to accept Morel's judgment on tactical details. He allowed the badge removal without apparent concern.

Waluigi notes: Morel controlled this moment. Morel decided when the badges came off. Morel decided who was 'involved.' This is not Bryan's operation — it is Morel's, with Bryan as the religious mandate provider and Dan as nominal motivation. Bryan believes he is leading. Waluigi suspects Morel is steering.

## The Shadowfell Grove — Last Known Location

Bryan, Dan, Morel, and a mage entered the Shadowfell through a portal Morel opened. They walked through Mazebound territory toward what they believed was Archie's location, following his Wahwire posts as an approximate tracker.

They were stopped by a Scorncrow — the grove's supernatural guardian. Bryan attempted peace. The Scorncrow rejected it. Bryan and Dan discussed going around. Dan insisted the path through the grove was the correct route.

They noticed the Mole and Morel had disappeared during this exchange.

Then: a massive fireball in the grove. The trees caught fire. Dan saw it and said 'that looks like Archie' with the specific recognition of someone who has watched Archie's fire before.

Waluigi cannot confirm whose fireball it was. If it was Archie's, Archie was in or near the grove at the time of the hunting party's arrival, and either sensed their presence or created the fire for entirely unrelated reasons. If it was someone else's, a third party with significant fire magic was operating in the same grove simultaneously.

Bryan's fate after the fireball is unconfirmed. The notes end there.

## Assessment

Bryan is a sincere person with a theological mandate and operationally limited situational awareness. He is being used by Mystic Morel as the authorizing principle for a hunt that Morel has been planning independently. He recruited Dan, who lied about his motives. He entered a hostile dimension without adequate intelligence.

None of this makes him less dangerous. A sincere Toad God servant who reaches Archie and believes divine judgment demands action will act. The sincerity is the threat.

Waluigi advises the party to understand Bryan before encountering him — he can be reasoned with if the reasoning addresses his theological framework rather than simply denying his conclusions. Arguing that Archie is not a threat will not work. Arguing that the Toad God's interests are better served by a different approach might.

This assumes Bryan is alive after the grove fireball. Waluigi does not yet know.

WAH.

faiths.note: Bryan serves a deity he calls the Toad God, and the Toad God agrees with the Cosmic Jester that the world is a thing to be bitten. Bryan arrived at the Raventree crisis with divine instruction and no Shadowfell experience whatsoever, which is the most Punchline-shaped situation the archive has recorded this year.

The Toad God ascended by fusing with a Crystal Star shard in the ashes of Edgeshade. Bryan's theology is therefore a Star Spirits heresy: the wish-granting stars are real, and one of them is now a person with a grievance.

name: Waluigi
title: The Great and Underappreciated
status: Active — concussed at Star Hill, 2 Aethel 1035: shot at over the lip of a rotor blade while using his own notebook as a shield; the working notebook is now in a courier's satchel and the archive holds one scrap of it
summary: Waluigi is the author of this encyclopedia, the greatest athlete in the Mushroom Kingdom, a master of ice magic and arcane rays, and the single most underappreciated individual in recorded history. He is tall, handsome, and possesses a sense of style that lesser beings cannot comprehend. This article is completely objective because Waluigi wrote it and Waluigi is incapable of bias regarding himself. The current party pass records Waluigi as field archivist, reluctant survivor, ice-magic specialist, and the only person sufficiently objective to explain why everyone else is wrong.
description:
While Mario gets parades and Luigi gets sympathy and Wario gets... whatever Wario gets (money, usually), Waluigi receives nothing but the satisfaction of knowing he is superior to everyone who overlooks him.

This is not bitterness. This is FACT.

## Current Party Pass: Field Archivist Under Protest

Waluigi's current role in the main-party file is obvious to anyone with taste: **field archivist, tactical commentator, and underappreciated survival specialist**. Unfortunately, the party keeps confusing this with "person to rescue after stepping into bear traps," which Waluigi considers defamatory even when technically accurate.

In the Feyward and Shadow Estate crisis chain, Waluigi has become more than comic relief, which Waluigi was never anyway. He is a live witness to Morel, Hjumpik's Asset Orange situation, Wario's mirror greed, Toad Lee's missing-time complications, and the manor's habit of turning architecture into attempted murder.

His ice magic and agility remain useful, but his true contribution is archival: Waluigi remembers details other people ignore, assigns blame with precision, and converts chaos into documentation sharp enough to hurt feelings.

## Public Inventory & Wallet Notes

Waluigi's public inventory remains deliberately opaque. This is not because Waluigi has nothing. This is because Waluigi is not a fool.

His operating wallet contains gold, silver, Midland Ducats, Guild Seals, Archive Writs, Arcane Shards, a Transit Stamp, Toad Whistle Tokens, and a Court Leaf. Translation: Waluigi carries research access, travel leverage, magical economy tokens, and enough conventional money to remain mobile. Unlike Wario, Waluigi understands that not all value is best stored as a pile you can sit on.

## Active Threads for Editors

- **Asset Unknown Purple:** the Guild's inability to categorize Waluigi remains hilarious and concerning.
- **Feyward survival:** injury, hag incidents, Morel pressure, and Hjumpik's cowbell all converge here.
- **Archive authority:** Waluigi is not just in the story; he is shaping how the story is remembered.
- **Wario coordination:** business partnership, betrayal irritation, and mirror-loot disputes remain active.

## Athletic Excellence

Waluigi has competed in every sporting event the Mushroom Kingdom has ever hosted and has been ROBBED of victory in approximately ninety percent of them. The referees are biased. The scoring systems are rigged. The other competitors—particularly a certain pair of PLUMBER BROTHERS—receive preferential treatment that would be scandalous if anyone bothered to investigate.

Despite this institutional opposition, Waluigi has achieved remarkable athletic success through sheer determination and physical gifts that include exceptional height, superior reflexes, and legs that can kick a tennis ball through a CASTLE WALL. Waluigi's specialty is tennis, though he excels at go-karting, party games, soccer, baseball, golf, and any other competition that allows him to demonstrate his obvious supremacy.

## Magical Capabilities

Waluigi's magical abilities have proven critical during the 1040 BF crisis. His ice magic—capable of freezing web structures, creating frozen corridors through hostile terrain, and shattering obstacles—was instrumental during the Battle of the Spider Grove. His arcane rays weakened the Arachnid Matriarch during the final phase of that engagement, targeting joint structures and contributing directly to the banishment victory.

These magical capabilities are ENTIRELY self-taught, which makes them more impressive than the pampered spellcasting of Mages' Guild graduates who learned their craft in COMFORTABLE TOWERS with INDOOR PLUMBING. Waluigi learned magic the hard way—through experimentation, failure, and the refusal to accept that anything is beyond his reach.

## The Edgeshade Incident

Waluigi must address the ALLEGATIONS regarding Edgeshade. Yes, Waluigi and Wario were present when dragons destroyed the town. No, this was not ENTIRELY their fault. The dragons were ALREADY angry about something—probably unrelated to anything Waluigi or Wario may or may not have done involving eggs, treasure, or territorial disputes. The official Kingdom investigation remains ongoing, and Waluigi maintains his innocence while acknowledging that perhaps, in HINDSIGHT, certain actions could have been reconsidered.

The destruction of Edgeshade has heightened security concerns across the Midlands, increased travel restrictions, and made Waluigi's movements somewhat more... complicated. This is FINE. Waluigi adapts. Waluigi overcomes. Waluigi does NOT accept responsibility for collateral damage caused by creatures with their OWN decision-making capabilities.

## Role in the Current Crisis

Waluigi has been an active participant in the events surrounding Raventree Manor, the Planar Fracture, and the multi-dimensional catastrophe that has scattered Disaster Inc. across hostile planes. His contributions include:

- Clearing paths with ice magic during the Spider Grove rescue operation
- Providing sustained arcane ray fire during the Arachnid Matriarch engagement
- Surviving the Planar Fracture and maintaining operational effectiveness in the Feywild
- Navigating Lady Aurelian Corvinarus's fey court without accidentally selling his soul, shadow, or naming rights
- Documenting the entire crisis through this encyclopedia, which future historians will recognize as the definitive account

Waluigi is currently trapped in the Feywild with Toad Lee, dealing with fairy politics that make Mushroom Kingdom diplomacy look straightforward. He is handling this situation with characteristic grace, determination, and only moderate amounts of screaming into pillows when nobody is watching.

## Personal Philosophy

Waluigi's worldview can be summarized simply: the universe owes Waluigi recognition, the universe has failed to provide that recognition, and Waluigi will TAKE what is owed through excellence so undeniable that even the biased machinery of reality cannot ignore it.

This is not arrogance. Arrogance is unearned confidence. Waluigi's confidence is EXTREMELY earned through decades of athletic achievement, magical development, and survival against odds that would have crushed lesser individuals. Waluigi has fought dragons (indirectly, and they started it). Waluigi has battled giant spiders (directly). Waluigi has endured fairy court politics (EXHAUSTINGLY). What has MARIO done lately? Jumped on a turtle? WAH.

## Relationships

Waluigi's primary partnership is with Wario, his business associate and the only person Waluigi trusts with money. Wario is greedy, loud, smells like garlic, and recently FAKED HIS OWN DEATH without telling Waluigi, which Waluigi is STILL annoyed about. But Wario is also HONEST about what he is, which Waluigi respects more than the false nobility of so-called heroes.

Waluigi's relationship with the rest of Disaster Inc. is complicated. He respects Markop's combat capabilities. He tolerates Archie's pyromania (from a safe distance of at least thirty feet). He appreciates Remi's determination. He finds the Oracle mysterious in ways that are either intriguing or infuriating depending on the day. He considers Green T a kindred spirit—someone who has been underestimated, dismissed, and ultimately proven MORE dangerous than anyone expected.

Waluigi's relationship with Luigi is... Waluigi does not wish to discuss his relationship with Luigi. The article is over. WAH.

## Latest Feyward Filing

Waluigi filed the Feyward escape in first person, claiming the OC Soul Ring after a garlic grenade and Bob-omb broke the plant-lady’s cage. He insists the disguise kit remains evidence of genius, not desperation.

## Regency Rescue File: Still Superstars

The Garden Above the Fire is one of the rare filings where Waluigi cannot hide behind being merely the author. He was there, he asked for the courier note's wording, and he answered Luigi's broken question when Mario was absent: *We are still superstars.* Waluigi files that line as evidence, not decoration — evidence that the rescue worked before the mystery did.

**Backfilled from 2 Aethel, 1035 BF — the loss of the notebook.** The helicopter leg from the outpost ended on a storehouse roof beside Star Hill Clinic, with Waluigi's working notebook — burns, brothers, the garden above the fire, verse — two fingers from going out of the open side door. He kept it through the crash, a stairwell that grew, a pistol in his face and a bluff of 'one per cent of my capacity' made with no MP at all, three copies of Mr. L on the stairs, and a fire-ladder retreat ('We are giving up on the Star-a Clinic'). He lost it in the street: he ran with it held up as a shield, the courier's shot took the lip off a rotor blade by his ear, and he went down. Wario threw the book to the gunman while he was out. He woke mid-verse with his own line still in his head, screamed, and asked the street WHO TOOK MY-A NOTEBOOK. The answer is a courier named Paulo. The archive holds one scrap, from the back of the book, recovered from a thorn. It is not about Luigi.

faiths.note: The Cult of WAH holds that everyone is cheating but you. Waluigi did not found it, does not collect from it, and has filed a formal objection to the name in his own encyclopedia — but he did articulate the doctrine, at length, to a god, while strapped to an electric chair. The congregation considers this scripture. WAH.

name: Orvinder Danos
title: The Barrister Who Cannot Lie
status: Active — last seen at a portal in the Shadowfell, affiliation with 'Usk' unclear
affiliation: Independent / Raventree Manor (formerly) / Unknown dimensional interests
summary:
Orvinder Danos is a thin, handsome man with neat dark hair, a mustache, bright keen eyes, and a cane he does not actually need. His clothing is clean, well-tailored, and deliberately plain—high quality without ornamentation, the wardrobe of someone who wants to project competence without flash. He appeared in the Shadowfell near the Purple Legion's crash site, knew Archie Miser by name without being told, offered portal access to the ruined manor, and introduced Archie to a being called 'Usk' who claimed to be split between three manors and needed help reuniting. Orvinder's defining characteristic—confirmed through Archie's assessment—is that he DOES NOT LIE. He has made truth an integral part of his existence. He does not ask others to lie on his behalf. He believes the truth may hurt, but anything that can be destroyed by the truth probably deserves to be. In a crisis defined by deception, manipulation, and competing fabrications, a man who refuses to lie is either the most valuable ally imaginable or the most dangerous liability. WAH.

## Merged Duplicate Record Note

Orvinder Danos is a lawyer in the Shadowfell. Yes, really. He is a barrister who values truth, justice, and the law, which makes him the single most out-of-place entity in a dimension ruled by manipulative, blood-sucking vampires. He assisted Archie in finding a dimensional portal. Waluigi profoundly distrusts lawyers, especially ones who claim to be honest and don't charge exorbitant fees.
description:
Waluigi is documenting Orvinder Danos because the man appeared at a critical moment, offered assistance that proved genuine, and then vanished into dimensional complexity with an entity called 'Usk' in ways that Waluigi cannot fully explain.

## Character Assessment — Truth as Identity

Archie assessed Orvinder's character and found the following traits:

**Truthful.** Orvinder does not lie. This is not a policy or a habit—it is an IDENTITY. He made the decision at a young age to make truth integral to his existence. He does not ask others to lie on his behalf. He believes strongly that 'the truth may hurt, but anything that can be destroyed by the truth probably deserves to be.'

In a world where EVERYONE lies—the Regency, the Guild, the Legion, the Loyalists, the vampires, the fey—a person who refuses to lie is either refreshingly honest or dangerously naive. Orvinder appears to be the former.

**Just.** To Orvinder, nothing matters more than justice. Two key truths guide him: laws must be upheld universally, and unjust laws must be changed into just ones. He has dedicated his life to learning the mechanisms by which both can be achieved.

**Witty.** Dry humor and sarcasm deployed with precision. He is charming in the specific way that legal professionals are charming—disarming enough to navigate noble courts, sharp enough to win arguments.

**Brave.** He takes cases defending common folk against the powerful. He does not waver when the powerful lean on him. This bravery is not physical—it is institutional. He fights with arguments and precedents rather than swords.

**Generous.** He pays his servants well, charges little to those who cannot afford his services, and lives frugally. Generosity in service of justice.

This combination—truthful, just, brave, generous—describes either a genuinely good person or the most sophisticated cover identity ever constructed. Waluigi's instinct says the former. Waluigi's experience says verify.

## The Shadowfell Appearance — How Did He Get There?

Orvinder appeared near the Purple Legion's crash site in the Shadowfell. He introduced himself as 'Orvinder Danos, Barrister' and asked 'Might you be Archie Miser?'

He knew Archie's name. He was in the SHADOWFELL—a dimension that most people cannot reach intentionally, let alone navigate casually. He walked with a cane he didn't need—a prop that suggests performance rather than disability.

His explanation: he was from Raventree Manor, was there until the Mages' Guild 'caged' him, and he had portal capabilities at 'certain reflection points.'

The portal ability is significant. Moving between dimensions through reflection points—mirrors, water surfaces, polished stone—is consistent with the mirror-based dimensional magic that defines Raventree Manor's planar nexus. If Orvinder can open portals at reflective surfaces, he has capabilities that rival the Oracle's dimensional manipulation.

## Usk — The Split Being

Orvinder introduced Archie to 'Usk'—an entity who claimed to be split between three manors and needed help reuniting all versions of themselves into one.

Usk's nature is unclear. They could be:
- A being fractured by the Planar Fracture, existing simultaneously in the Material, Shadowfell, and Feywild fragments
- A dimensional entity native to the spaces between planes
- A construct or creation of the Oracle or the Corvinarus family
- Something else entirely

Orvinder's association with Usk suggests deeper involvement in the dimensional crisis than his barrister persona implies. Lawyers typically do not manage interdimensional reunification projects.

Archie declined to help immediately—'I'm looking for my friends'—and Orvinder accepted this gracefully, promising to 'talk to Usk and meet you up later.'

## The Shack Incident — Overheard Anger

Later, Archie encountered Orvinder and others at a shack where shouting was heard:

'...ARE YOU DOING!? We need to initiate the teleport—Shadeward to Faeward—get the portal up! If Archie hears about it, we're both screwed!'

The shouting individuals departed before Archie could confront them. This suggests that Orvinder's dimensional operations have aspects that Archie is not supposed to know about. The panic about Archie discovering the teleportation suggests that Archie's presence—or his entropy-bleeding magic—would interfere with whatever they were attempting.

## Waluigi's Assessment

Orvinder Danos is a truthful man operating in a crisis built on lies. His inability to deceive—if genuine—makes him uniquely valuable as a source of reliable information AND uniquely vulnerable to manipulation by those who CAN lie.

A man who cannot lie can still WITHHOLD truth. He can choose what to share and what to keep silent about. The truth he offers may be incomplete without being false. This is the lawyer's art: technical honesty deployed strategically.

Orvinder's dimensional capabilities, his association with Usk, and the overheard panic about Archie discovering their operations suggest involvement in events that extend beyond legal practice. He is either helping to fix the dimensional crisis or navigating it for purposes Waluigi cannot yet identify.

The cane he doesn't need bothers Waluigi. Why carry a prop? What does it represent? What does it conceal?

Orvinder Danos tells the truth. The question is whether the truth he tells is the WHOLE truth.

WAH.

## Merged Duplicate Record Note

Orvinder Danos looks exactly like a well-to-do merchant or noble: neat dark hair, a mustache, keen eyes, and well-tailored clothing that lacks flashy ornamentation. He walks with a cane he does not actually need, which Waluigi recognizes as a classic theatrical prop to make opponents underestimate you.

**The Honest Lawyer**
Orvinder's defining trait is that he does not lie. Ever. He believes that laws must be upheld universally and unjust laws must be changed. He defends common folk against nobles. In the Shadowfell, where deceit is the primary currency, a man who strictly tells the truth is either completely insane or so powerful that he doesn't need to lie. Waluigi leans toward the latter.

**Planar Capabilities**
Orvinder encountered Archie while Archie was disguised as a guard. Orvinder saw right through it. More importantly, Orvinder demonstrated a staggering magical capability: he can open planar portals at certain 'reflection points.' He opened a portal to the ruined physical manor for Archie, explaining that it takes immense concentration but allows transit across the boundaries the Oracle broke.

Orvinder also seems to be acting as a guide or protector for Usk, attempting to reunite Usk's fragmented essence across the three manors. Why a barrister is involving himself in dimensional rescue operations is unclear. Perhaps he considers the Planar Fracture a violation of cosmic law. 

Waluigi would rather fight three dragons than be cross-examined by Orvinder Danos in a courtroom. WAH.

faiths.note: A well-tailored man with a cane he does not need, plain clothing chosen to be forgettable, and dimensional interests nobody has mapped. Every visible choice Orvinder makes is about controlling what other people conclude. The archive files him here provisionally and expects to be surprised.

name: Green T
title: The Giant from the Children's Table
status: Active — followed the party to the TOADALNAEC to supervise, fired a gun at a gold toad to see whether it would bounce, and tipped the barrel with Archie in it back toward the door while Markop kept Rivers talking
summary:
Green T is the most impressive individual Waluigi has encountered during the entire 1040 BF crisis, and Waluigi does not say that lightly because Waluigi has encountered HIMSELF during this crisis. Green T ran a criminal empire with the demeanor of a garden party host, survived its complete destruction, was dragged through a mirror dimension, reappeared in the Shadowfell, got insulted to the children's table at a vampire dinner party, and used that insult as cover to shoot a vampire lord with a silver bullet. His story is proof that being underestimated is a weapon, and Waluigi—who has been underestimated his entire life—finds that deeply inspiring.

Green T’s newest Shadow Estate entry is not about pretending to know things. In fact, he specifically admitted he did not know where the mirror was, which Waluigi reluctantly respects because honesty is cheaper than being wrong loudly. Green T coordinated the mirror base and fragment handoff, received the repaired Mirror of True Reflection into temporary custody, and now holds it under a bargain in which Wario expects to claim it after Scarecrow is killed.
description:
Green T was the leader of the Tea Leaf Syndicate, which operated aboard the Vigilance as the classiest criminal organization Waluigi has ever encountered. The Syndicate served excellent tea, maintained tasteful décor, and conducted criminal enterprises with an aesthetic sensibility that Waluigi respected enormously. Green T ran this operation with supernatural calm—meetings were conducted over tea, threats were delivered with impeccable politeness, and violence was reserved for situations where other options had been exhausted.

Nobody knew Green T could turn into a giant.

NOBODY.

## The Transformation

During the Syndicate Showdown—the final confrontation that destroyed the Tea Leaf Syndicate—Green T revealed a capability that nobody had suspected. When the fighting started, Green T GREW. Not just bigger—ENORMOUS. His body expanded until he filled the corridor like a living wall, and he used that massive form to crush an Iron Legion soldier with a single blow.

Waluigi's jaw dropped. Waluigi's jaw does NOT drop easily. But watching the calm tea merchant who had always seemed like the most reasonable person in any room transform into a TITAN was one of the most shocking moments of the campaign. Green T had been hiding this ability the ENTIRE TIME—running a criminal empire, hosting meetings, serving tea—while possessing the power to become a colossus.

The restraint this represents is remarkable. Green T COULD have used his giant form to crush enemies, intimidate rivals, or dominate through raw physical power. Instead, he kept it hidden, using it only when the Syndicate's existence was already ending. That's discipline. That's strategy. That's the kind of long-term thinking that Waluigi aspires to but rarely achieves because Waluigi's emotions are POWERFUL and IMMEDIATE.

## The Mirror Dimension

Green T's story took a dark turn during the Siege of Raventree Manor when a glass monster emerged from one of the manor's mirrors and targeted him specifically. During the chaos, the entity seized Green T and pulled him bodily through a mirror surface into a mirror dimension—a layer of reflected reality that existed alongside the physical world.

Witnesses described it as violent and instantaneous. One moment Green T was there. The next, he was gone—dragged through glass like someone being pulled underwater. The mirror surface rippled, then went still, reflecting only an empty hallway.

Green T was presumed lost. Another casualty of Raventree Manor's supernatural hostility. Another victim of a building that eats people through its own décor.

Then he reappeared in the Shadowfell.

## The Shadow Estate Dinner

Green T's presence at the Shadow Estate dinner party is itself remarkable—he had been dragged through a mirror dimension, transited through unknown planar layers, and emerged in the Shadowfell's reflection of the manor, apparently intact and ready to cause problems for vampires. Waluigi does not know the details of this journey. Green T has not been forthcoming. What matters is that he SURVIVED when survival seemed impossible.

At the dinner, the vampire lords placed Green T at the children's table. This was intended as an insult—a dismissal of someone they considered beneath the dignity of adult conversation. The vampires saw a survivor, a refugee from the broken Tea Leaf Syndicate, someone with no faction backing and no obvious threat capability.

This was the single greatest mistake they could have made.

Green T used the insult as cover. While the vampires focused their attention on Archie's diplomatic performance at the main table, Green T spent the dinner observing, planning, and preparing. He mapped the room. He identified exits and guard positions. He waited for the exact moment when everyone's attention was elsewhere.

Then he stood up from the children's table, produced a firearm loaded with silver bullets—how he smuggled it into a vampire dinner party remains unexplained—and shot Orangus Cornelius, the senior vampire lord, in front of everyone.

THE CHILDREN'S TABLE SHOT THE HOST.

Waluigi WISHES he could have seen Orangus's face. The moment of comprehension when a centuries-old vampire lord realized he'd dismissed the most dangerous person in the room to sit with the CHILDREN. The fraction of a second between 'this cannot be happening' and 'this is absolutely happening.'

## Assessment

Green T is what Waluigi aspires to be: someone who gets knocked down repeatedly, loses everything, and comes back MORE dangerous each time. He lost his organization to Archie's fireball and Earl Grey's explosion. He lost his freedom to the mirror dimension. He lost any pretense of belonging to a faction or having backup. And yet he kept going—surviving, adapting, and ultimately delivering one of the most satisfying moments of the entire campaign.

Waluigi respects very few people unconditionally. Green T has earned that respect. He is proof that being underestimated is not a weakness—it's a weapon. And Waluigi, who has been underestimated his entire life, finds that deeply, personally meaningful.

Waluigi would buy Green T a drink. Several drinks. And then Waluigi would ask him how he smuggled that gun into the dinner party, because Waluigi NEEDS to know. WAH.

## Recent Update — Temporary Mirror Custodian

After the mirror base and fragment were recovered, Green T became the practical custodian of the restored Mirror of True Reflection. This is not the same as ownership. Wario has opinions about ownership. Waluigi has opinions about Wario’s opinions. The important part is that the artifact is no longer broken and is currently in party control while the portal circle remains occupied by Tanukiburt, Toadburt, and Mystic Morel.

**Latest Filing (1040 BF):** Appeared as a giant during the Scorncrow Skirmish, offering Remi a shoulder ride to act as a spotter.

## Returned to Play — Sheet Filed

Green T is back on the table this session, so the archive now carries a playable record and not only a dossier. He runs as a level 6 giant-blooded tea merchant: the giant form, the concealed revolver, and a calm that people keep mistaking for harmlessness.

The comeback is the whole character. He was taken through a mirror at Raventree and filed as a casualty. He came back through the Shadowfell, was seated at the children's table as an insult, and shot the senior vampire lord with silver. Waluigi wants the record to be honest that the archive was wrong about him twice — once when it counted him dead, and once when it assumed the giant form was a win condition rather than something that spends the body holding it. The grove corrected the second error in public.

Playable sheet: `tools/item sheet examples/fvtt-Actor-green-t-level-6-giant-player.json`, generated by `tools/build-green-t-actor.py`.
