description:
Waluigi is writing Remi's full record because the archive contains extensive documentation of what Remi does and insufficient documentation of who Remi is and how she got here. The how she got here is important. The who she is becomes more legible when you know where she started and what she crossed to get to where she ended up.

Waluigi wants to note upfront that reconstructing Remi's backstory involves cross-referencing her own accounts  which are vivid, emotionally accurate, and occasionally inconsistent on dates  with corroborating sources Waluigi has been able to locate. Remi is not a liar. She is a narrator whose attention to the things that matter to her is total and whose attention to logistical detail is approximate. Waluigi has done his best.

## Current Party Pass: Engineer-Witness of the Crisis

Remi's current role is not merely "the new one" or "the girl from the barrel." Waluigi updates her classification to **engineer-witness**: the person whose tools, memory, weapon, and testimony increasingly connect the Shadow Estate's machinery to the party's survival.

She is armed again, skeptical for excellent reasons, and far better at practical troubleshooting than most adults who keep calling themselves experts. Remi has already handled intruders, reclaimed agency after captivity, tested dangerous truth/lie logic around the Black Crystal, and continued thinking like an engineer while surrounded by people who treat evidence like a throwable object.

The **Oracle's Deck** remains narratively radioactive. It is not simply an item in Remi's possession; it is a pressure point linking her to prophecy, Mystic Morel, and decisions no child should have to carry. Waluigi is filing this prominently because fate likes to hide behind accessories.

## Public Inventory & Wallet Notes

Remi's public inventory includes the **Oracle's Deck** and one spoiler-safe hidden belongings concern. The hidden slot matters because Remi's left-behind property, firearm history, and Shadow Estate custody all intersect with agency. Waluigi will not reduce that to "lost item."

Her field wallet is more complex than most party members: **Kivotos Credits**, **Credsticks**, **Data Chits**, gold, silver, Midland Ducats, Toad Whistle Tokens, Mushroom Coin, and Relief Stamps. Translation for non-bankers: Remi has a cross-world engineer's wallet, not a peasant purse. Some of it spends in ordinary markets. Some of it is institutional credit. Some of it is proof that Kivotos followed her farther than expected.

## Active Threads for Editors

- **Oracle's Deck:** prophecy, pressure, and Morel-adjacent manipulation.
- **Engineering role:** Remi is now one of the party's strongest links to machines, schematics, repairs, and evidence handling.
- **Shadow Estate testimony:** her observations are operational intelligence, not side commentary.
- **Kivotos connection:** her money, background, and tech literacy all point back to a world that is not finished with her.

## Kivotos: The City That Runs on Academy Girls

Kivotos is a city-state that Waluigi has spent considerable time documenting from the outside because the inside is difficult to access without being enrolled in one of its academies or affiliated organizations. The city operates on a system that would be considered unusual by most political frameworks: it is run almost entirely by students. Academy students, specifically, organized into schools that function simultaneously as educational institutions, paramilitary factions, law enforcement bodies, and the primary governance mechanism for a city of considerable size and complexity.

The Kivotos Student Council and affiliated academy committees exist as coordinating bodies for inter-academy relations and city-wide security, but the actual day-to-day operation of the city  law enforcement, infrastructure, commerce, emergency response  falls to the academies and their students. This system has produced a city where teenagers negotiate territorial disputes, conduct criminal investigations, and maintain armed standing forces, while simultaneously attending classes.

Waluigi finds Kivotos fascinating and slightly terrifying. It is a city that has decided, at a systemic level, that its young people are its most capable citizens. Whether this is a genuine recognition of extraordinary capability or an elaborate rationalization for not having to pay adults is a question Waluigi has not resolved. What Waluigi has resolved is that growing up in Kivotos produces a specific kind of person: someone who is accustomed to institutions being real and consequential, who understands that schools have power, and who has learned to navigate factional politics before they are old enough to have developed the cynicism that usually accompanies that knowledge.

Remi was born in Kivotos on the 12th of Harvestide, 1026 BF. She grew up in Residential District Seven, which is not affiliated with any major academy  a gap in the city's institutional coverage that produced a specific kind of childhood. She knew the academies existed. She could see their banners from her bedroom window. She was not in one.

## The Akamatsu Family: What Waluigi Has Been Able to Confirm

Remi's family name is Akamatsu. Waluigi has partial records, and the gaps in those records are informative.

Her parents were not affiliated with any major academy faction. In Kivotos, this is not unusual for residents of the unaffiliated residential districts  people live in the city, work in the city, and maintain an existence adjacent to the academy system without being inside it. The Akamatsu family existed in this space, which is comfortable when the academies are operating smoothly and increasingly uncomfortable when they are not.

Remi has spoken about her family in the scattered way that people speak about things they are trying not to think about too directly. From these fragments, Waluigi has assembled the following: there were parents, there was a home in District Seven with a window that faced the Gehenna Academy towers, there was a period of relative normality that ended sometime before Remi turned eleven. The specific nature of the ending is something Remi has not disclosed in any documented session. She describes the period before as 'when things were normal' and does not elaborate on what normal contained or when it stopped.

What Waluigi can say is that Remi arrived at Gehenna Academy without a family escort, which is unusual for new students. She was processed as an independent enrollment. She listed her emergency contact as her own name. The academy administrators noted this under 'irregular' and apparently did not follow up, which tells Waluigi something about Gehenna Academy's administrative priorities and something about how thoroughly Remi had already learned to present self-sufficiency as a complete answer to questions about support systems.

Waluigi is not going to speculate beyond what the record supports about what happened to the Akamatsu family. The record supports: they were present, then they were not present enough, and Remi enrolled in Gehenna Academy at age twelve as an independent student with herself listed as her own emergency contact. Whatever the gap contains, Remi crossed it before she crossed the Firewall Gate, and both crossings required the same skill: moving forward when the thing behind you is no longer a direction you can go.

## Gehenna Academy: Eight Months

Gehenna Academy is one of Kivotos's established academic institutions with an organizational culture oriented around discipline, hierarchy, and a specific kind of dangerous elegance. Its students are known for being capable, difficult, and very good at things that polite society pretends not to need. The academy's aesthetic runs toward controlled darkness  not cruelty exactly, but the specific sharpness of an institution that has decided that softness is a liability and has built its entire culture around that decision.

Remi enrolled at Gehenna at age twelve. Standard enrollment for her track. She was not flagged as exceptional in ways that enrollment records highlight  not a scholarship student, not noted as a discipline problem in intake documentation, not identified for special programs. She was a student who showed up, attended classes, and existed in the specific way that students without family waiting at home exist: with a self-containment that can look like independence and is often loneliness with better posture.

Gehenna was not a bad fit for Remi, and this is important to document because it would be easy to assume that a twelve-year-old orphaned or near-orphaned student who ended up alone in a barrel would have been miserable at an academy. She was not miserable. She was adequate in most subjects. She was better than adequate at moving through spaces without being noticed, which Gehenna's culture rewards without formally teaching. She understood hierarchy intuitively because she had been navigating a city of competing institutional hierarchies her entire childhood without being inside any of them. Gehenna's internal politics were complicated but legible to someone who had been watching academy politics from the outside since she could see the towers from her window.

She made acquaintances. Waluigi uses acquaintances deliberately rather than friends because the distinction matters. Friends are people who would have noticed she was gone. Acquaintances are people who would eventually mention she seemed to have stopped coming to class.

She was at Gehenna for eight months before the circumstances that led to the barrel.

## The Circumstances That Led to Leaving Kivotos

Waluigi is going to document this section with appropriate precision while acknowledging the limits of available sources. Remi's own account of this period is her most fragmented self-narrative  she describes it in images rather than sequences, in impressions rather than events. What can be confirmed from external sources is limited. What can be inferred from the trajectory is more.

Kivotos in 1038-1039 BF was experiencing inter-academy tension that periodically destabilizes the city's cooperative governance structure. The relevant context for Remi specifically: she was an unaffiliated student at Gehenna Academy during a period when the unaffiliated spaces in the city were more contested than usual.

Remi encountered something she should not have encountered. She was in a place she was not supposed to be at a time when being in that place carried consequences. Waluigi cannot determine from available sources what specifically she saw or knew. What is clear from the trajectory: whatever it was, it attached consequences to her continued presence in Kivotos. Not immediate violence  Remi would not have had time to plan if it had been immediate violence. A slower-building problem. The kind that gives you enough warning to make choices but not enough safety to stay and fight it.

She left Gehenna without formal withdrawal. Not through any process. She left in the specific way that people leave situations when the alternative to leaving is worse than the complications of going  quickly, with what she could carry in a bag that was too heavy for her to carry with one hand, without telling anyone where she was going because she did not know where she was going.

She did not go back to District Seven. Whatever the family situation was, it was not a direction that remained open. Waluigi notes this without elaborating beyond what the record supports: she did not go back.

She went to the edge of Kivotos instead. Which in 1038 BF meant approaching the boundary of the physical realm and the beginning of the Internet region  the digital territory that lies east of the Midlands, between Kivotos and the rest of the physical world.

And then she had to figure out how to cross it.

## The Great Firewall Gate: How a Twelve-Year-Old Crossed

The Great Firewall Gate is the primary entry point from the physical realm into the Internet  a colossal, shimmering barrier of pure data where all traffic is inspected by Internet Federation sentinels. The Gate is not unpassable. It is simply not passable without the right documentation, the right affiliation, or the right combination of being small enough and unremarkable enough that the sentinels' pattern-matching protocols categorize you as background noise.

Remi was twelve. She had a Gehenna Academy student identification card, which she no longer had active enrollment to support. She had the contents of a bag that was too heavy to carry with one hand. She had no Internet Federation transit pass, no diplomatic clearance, no data-packet registration, and no adult.

Waluigi has attempted to reconstruct how she got through the Gate. The most complete explanation, assembled from fragments of Remi's account and what Waluigi knows about Gate operations in 1038-1039 BF, is this:

The Gate sentinels run pattern-matching on incoming entities. Students from affiliated academies transit regularly for educational purposes  field trips, research exchanges, approved digital learning programs. Gehenna Academy has an approved educational transit category. A twelve-year-old in Gehenna Academy colors carrying a student identification card triggers the 'academy student, educational transit' pattern before the sentinel runs the enrollment verification check.

The verification check takes approximately forty-five seconds.

Remi moved through the Gate during shift change. Waluigi cannot confirm whether this was deliberate or fortunate. Remi's account of this moment is: 'I walked through when nobody was watching the gap.' This is either tactical awareness or twelve-year-old opportunism. The outcome is the same either way: the enrollment verification ran on a sentinel who was in transition, the flag it would have generated went to an in-progress console, and Remi was categorized as Gate Exemption 7-C  academy student in transit, no further action required  and processed through.

She was on the Surface Web before anyone noticed the exemption should not have been issued.

Waluigi finds this simultaneously impressive and deeply concerning. The Great Firewall Gate's reputation for impregnability is, apparently, conditional on the shift change being staffed correctly. Waluigi is filing this as security intelligence.

## The Surface Web: Three Weeks Alone

The Surface Web is the largest and most navigable portion of the Internet region. It contains the Oracle's Spire  the impossibly tall central index where archivists and algorithms answer any question for a price  the Great Social Forum where billions share their lives and manufacture misinformation simultaneously, the Agora of Memes where Reddit-adjacent chaos generates cultural currency at unpredictable intervals, and dozens of other major nodes ranging from the professionally sterile LinkedIn Professional Spire to the Anonymity Cauldron where the Cosmic Jesters operate in unstable and largely inadvisable conditions.

Remi spent approximately three weeks crossing the Surface Web on foot. Alone. At twelve years old. With a bag that was too heavy to carry with one hand.

Waluigi wants to document this period with the full attention it deserves because it is the period that most directly explains who Remi is when she arrives on the Vigilance, and the period that most directly shapes the operational capabilities that Disaster Inc. has come to rely on without fully understanding where they came from.

### The Oracle's Spire: The First Stop

The Oracle's Spire is the Internet Federation's central knowledge index  a gleaming, impossibly tall structure where the Cybernetic Collectives maintain archivists and algorithms capable of answering any question, for a price. The price varies depending on the question's classification and the requester's affiliation. For unaffiliated travelers with no Federation credentials, the price is typically 'tell us who you are and where you came from.'

Remi did not tell them who she was or where she came from. She did something more effective: she asked questions that had free-tier answers. The Oracle's Spire, like most knowledge institutions, maintains a public access level. Basic geographic queries. Transit routes. General information about the political landscape of the regions she was crossing. She sat in the public terminals of the Spire's lobby for most of a day, asking free-tier questions about the Midlands and the physical realm beyond the Internet's eastern border, and left before anyone thought to ask about her credentials.

What she learned: the Midlands region was accessible from the Internet's eastern boundary through three primary transit nodes. The most commonly used was the ISP Toll-Bridge, controlled by the Data Merchant Guilds, which charged a transit fee calibrated to a traveler's apparent resource level. The second was a smaller, unmonitored passage through the Cookie Cache Caverns that the Hacktivist Collectives used for unofficial transit  dangerous due to identity theft risk but free. The third was the Regal Empire Digital Embassy transit access, which required Imperial affiliation documentation and was therefore inaccessible to Remi.

She noted all three. She decided on the ISP Toll-Bridge because it was the most legitimate and because legitimate channels, in her experience, were easier to navigate than dangerous unofficial ones when you were small and unremarkable enough to be processed as routine.

First, she had to get from the Spire to the Toll-Bridge, which meant crossing the Social Forum, the Agora of Memes, and the western edge of the Surface Web on foot.

### The Great Social Forum: The Week She Spent Not Being Found

The Great Social Forum is a chaotic, sprawling city of interconnected platforms where users share thoughts, news, and pictures of their meals simultaneously. It is a hotbed of political debate, a misinformation engine, and the most densely populated node in the Surface Web. It is also, for reasons that have to do with the Forum's fundamental architecture, extremely easy to disappear into.

The Forum runs on attention. Data entities that generate engagement are amplified. Data entities that generate no engagement are effectively invisible. A twelve-year-old girl crossing the Forum without posting, interacting, or engaging with any of the platform's content is, from the Forum's perspective, not there. The sentinels who patrol the Forum's major corridors are optimized for flagging high-engagement threats  misinformation campaigns, flame wars, coordinated harassment operations. A quiet, unremarkable transit generates nothing for their pattern-matching to catch.

Remi crossed the Forum in approximately a week. She slept in one of the Forum's unmonitored server closets on the third night  Waluigi does not have a cleaner explanation  and ate from the Forum's food distribution nodes, which supply sustenance for the Forum's resident population and do not require registration to access at the basic tier.

She watched the Forum operate around her for seven days. She watched how information moved. She watched how attention worked. She watched how entities performing one thing were often doing something entirely different underneath the performance, and how the Forum's architecture made the performance more real than whatever was underneath it.

Waluigi suspects this week is where Remi developed  or perhaps recognized in herself  the instinct for performance that has characterized her behavior throughout the Raventree operation. The ghost-luring dance. The watermelon execution. The way she turns threat into theater. The Forum is a city that runs entirely on performance. A week inside it, observing, would teach anyone who was paying attention that performance is the primary currency of social reality. Remi was paying attention. She always is.

### The Agora of Memes: Forty-Eight Hours of the Most Chaotic Place on the Surface Web

The Agora of Memes is the Surface Web node that most closely approximates chaos as an architectural principle. Reddit-adjacent in structure, it contains forums dedicated to every topic imaginable, organized into communities that maintain their own internal governance with varying degrees of sanity. The Agora generates viral content, new ideas, and mob action in roughly equal proportions. Its security is inconsistent  some communities are tightly policed, others have no moderation at all, and the zones between communities are contested territory where anything can happen.

Remi passed through the Agora because it was on the route between the Forum and the ISP Toll-Bridge and she did not have an alternative that was shorter.

She spent approximately forty-eight hours crossing it. Waluigi's sources on this period are primarily Remi's own account, which is vivid in some places and entirely absent in others. What she describes: a community that recognized her Gehenna Academy colors and tried to recruit her for a faction dispute that she did not understand and did not participate in. A node moderator who noticed she was unaffiliated and offered to register her as a community member, which she declined because registration requires identification. A section of the Agora where the Cosmic Jesters had been active recently and the data landscape was still unstable from whatever they had done there  she describes it as 'the ground kept trying to be something different than a ground.'

She describes coming out the other side with her bag slightly lighter because she had traded some of her food supplies for transit information from an Agora regular who knew the Toll-Bridge's shift patterns. This is the first documented instance of Remi trading information for information. She did it instinctively, without framing it as a transaction, in the way that people do things instinctively when those things are what they are naturally good at.

### The ISP Toll-Bridge: The Price of Transit

The ISP Toll-Bridge is a heavily fortified data bridge controlled by a Data Merchant Guild monopoly. All traffic must pass through and pay a toll calibrated to the traveler's apparent resources. Premium subscribers move faster. Non-subscribers are throttled. Unregistered travelers without any data identity on record are assessed at the entry point and charged based on the evaluating agent's assessment of their value.

Remi had no data identity. She had a Gehenna Academy card that was no longer valid. She had some remaining food supplies, some Kivotos currency whose exchange rate in the Internet region was negligible, and a bag that was too heavy to carry with one hand.

The evaluating agent looked at her for a long moment. Looked at the bag. Looked at the student card.

Remi told the evaluating agent that she was a Gehenna Academy student on a field research trip, that her group had gotten separated at the Forum, and that she needed to reach the physical realm before her supervisor filed a missing student report with the Internet Federation, which would be very complicated for everyone involved including the Toll-Bridge operator who had allowed her to be held up at the Gate for this long.

Waluigi wants to examine this statement carefully because it is the first fully documented instance of Remi's primary social capability deployed in a high-stakes context: she constructed a narrative that was entirely false, delivered it with the specific confidence of someone who genuinely believed what they were saying, and included in it a consequence for the other party that made compliance easier than resistance.

The missing student report. A filing with the Internet Federation. Complicated for everyone including the Toll-Bridge operator.

None of this was true. There was no supervisor. There was no group. There was no missing student report in progress. But the Toll-Bridge operator did not know that. And the Internet Federation, which regulates the Toll-Bridge's operations, is an entity that Toll-Bridge operators prefer to have no negative interactions with. The statement gave the operator a reason to let her through that was easier than the alternative.

The operator assessed her at a minimal toll  Waluigi suspects substantially below market rate, possibly even at the Bridge's 'student rate' which applies to affiliated Academy students  and processed her through.

She crossed into the physical realm's eastern boundary.

Waluigi is documenting this incident in full because it is the prototype for every social interaction Remi has had since: she constructs a narrative, she delivers it as though it is true, and she gives the other party a reason to comply that is easier than whatever the alternative is. It works more often than it should. It sometimes fails catastrophically. The ratio has been approximately the same since she was twelve years old crossing a toll bridge with a forged student card and a story about a missing field trip group.

## The Physical Realm: From the Internet Border to the Midlands Coast

The eastern border of the Internet region connects to the physical realm at several transit points. The one closest to the Toll-Bridge exit is not near any major settlement  it is a border station with minimal staffing, designed primarily for data-cargo transit rather than physical traveler processing. Remi emerged from the Internet border station into physical realm territory that was, by her assessment, very flat, very gray, and very far from anything recognizable.

She was twelve years old, on foot, in the physical realm's eastern territories, approximately three hundred miles from the nearest Midlands port.

She walked. And rode when she could. And walked when she couldn't ride. And occasionally talked her way onto cargo wagons with stories about field trips and separated groups and supervisors who would be very concerned about filing reports. She had approximately three weeks of physical-realm transit before she reached the Midlands coast, during which time she developed a set of capabilities that Waluigi has been observing in action for the entire Raventree operation without knowing their origin:

The ability to assess strangers quickly and identify what story will work on them. The ability to be unremarkable enough in a crowd to move through it unnoticed. The ability to sleep in small uncomfortable spaces and emerge from them functional. The ability to trade information for other information. The ability to evaluate a situation's risk in motion, while still in the situation, and adjust without giving any external signal that adjustment is occurring.

These are not skills Remi was taught. These are skills she developed by spending a month alone in transit through the Internet region and the physical realm's eastern territories at age twelve. They are the skills of someone who learned that the difference between arriving safely and not arriving at all was usually a question of what story you told and how much you believed it while you were telling it.

Waluigi finds this foundational to understanding Remi's paradox: she is, simultaneously, someone with sophisticated social and infiltration capabilities that she has been developing since age twelve, and someone who nearly signed an enthrallment contract because the guard seemed friendly. These facts are not contradictory. The social capabilities she developed were defensive and forward-moving  for getting through gates, onto wagons, across bridges. She never developed the parallel skill of recognizing when someone else is running a narrative on her. She learned to be the one telling the story. She never built the reflex of asking whether the story is being told at her.

The Shadow Estate has been exploiting this gap systematically. Vostolas exploited it with a birthday party. Mystic Morel exploited it with a ring. The Onyx Hand has been exploiting it with friendship contracts. Every exploitation uses the same mechanism: they tell Remi a story, they make the story appealing, and they rely on the fact that Remi has excellent story-telling instincts and poor story-receiving instincts.

The kneecap shot happened when Remi stopped receiving a story and started telling one of her own. 'That's what you get for pretending to be my friend.' Her story. Her terms. Her resolution.

Waluigi is watching for more moments like that one.

## The Midlands Coast and the Barrel

The Midlands coast is documented extensively elsewhere in the archive. For Remi's purposes, the relevant fact is that the Midlands coast in 1038-1039 BF was an active commercial shipping zone with regular cargo runs to various destinations including the Vigilance, which was at that point operating as a commercial trading hub as well as a mobile headquarters for the Liberated Toads.

Remi reached the Midlands coast after approximately three weeks of physical-realm transit. She was thin, tired, and significantly more competent than she had been when she left Kivotos. She had spent a month traveling through territories that required her to be competent in order to pass through them, and she had passed through them.

She spent approximately four days on the Midlands coast before she identified the cargo shipment bound for the Vigilance. The identification was not accidental. She had been asking questions at the docks in the same way she had asked questions at the Oracle's Spire's public terminals  free-tier queries, specific enough to be useful, vague enough not to trigger anything that would require her to identify herself. She learned that the Vigilance accepted commercial cargo. She learned that cargo was processed with lighter passenger scrutiny than direct passenger boarding. She found a barrel in a cargo staging area that was large enough to contain her and her bag if she arranged both carefully.

The barrel smelled like pickled things that had previously been in it and were no longer there. Remi describes this without particular emotion, which tells Waluigi more about what the preceding month had normalized than about the barrel specifically.

She got in. She arranged herself and the bag. She waited.

Four days of transit. She had food for four days because she had calculated the transit time from questions she had asked at the dock. The food was enough. The cold at altitude was not something she had fully accounted for and she describes the third day as 'very cold,' which is the most complaint she has offered about any part of this journey.

She emerged from the barrel onto the Vigilance cargo deck blinking and cramped and immediately grabbed by a crew member who was not expecting cargo to have a face.

The crew member  Eager, by most accounts, though at least one source says it was a different crew member and Eager arrived moments later  said: what in the 

Remi said: hi. I'm Remi. Is this the Vigilance.

It was.

## The Vigilance: FNG

FNG  Freaking New Guy, or the more profane version the Vigilance crew actually used  was applied to Remi within approximately forty minutes of her emergence from the barrel. This is how the Vigilance crew handled new arrivals whose status was unclear: you were FNG until you were something else. The designation carried no particular malice. It was administrative in the specific way that crew designations are administrative on vessels that need to track who belongs and who doesn't.

Remi was FNG for longer than most people. Not because she failed to prove herself  she proved herself in the specific ways that small, quiet, observant people prove themselves, by being useful in situations where those qualities are the most useful possible thing. She was FNG for longer because she was twelve years old on a vessel full of adults and former combatants, and the people who liked her could not quite bring themselves to stop thinking of her as the kid who came out of the barrel. The designation and the affection behind it were not always the same thing.

Waluigi wants to document what Remi's actual name contains and does not contain, because the FNG question deserves a complete answer.

Her name is Remi Akamatsu. FNG was never her name. It was a placeholder  the Vigilance crew's way of saying 'the new one' until she was something more specific. She was called FNG Remi by people who meant it as affection. She was called FNG Remi by people who meant it as dismissal. She was called Remi by the people who had decided she mattered. The progression from FNG Remi to Remi tracks approximately with the progression from cargo deck stowaway to something that might be called crew.

In Disaster Inc., she is Remi. The FNG designation did not follow her out of the Vigilance's operational sphere. What followed her was everything she learned while holding it.

What Remi did on the Vigilance:

She learned. The Vigilance was a better practical education than Gehenna's formal curriculum for the specific skills the next two years of her life would require. Cargo inventory. Basic navigation. How to move through a ship without being noticed by the people who would send her somewhere safer if they noticed her. How to listen to conversations not meant for her ears. How to assess whether a person presenting friendliness was actually friendly or was friendly toward a specific goal  this is the skill she learned in theory on the Vigilance but has had consistent difficulty applying in practice, particularly in supernatural environments designed to exploit exactly the gap where this skill should be.

She made something closer to friends than acquaintances  people whose continued existence she cared about, who would notice if she stopped coming to meals. The Toad contingent adopted her with the specific enthusiasm that toads apply to most things, which is total and immediate and not contingent on whether the recipient wants to be adopted. Remi did not resist adoption. She had been without it long enough that even Toad-style adoption was welcome.

She was present on the Vigilance during the Iron Sky Breach. She was twelve  nearly thirteen  when the Legion took the ship. She went into the chaos the way she had arrived on the ship: by finding a small space and being very quiet. She survived. She ended up outside the Vigilance's operational range in the post-Breach confusion, separated from the crew members she knew, navigating a situation with no clear next step.

Waluigi notes that 'I'm used to it'  what Luigi reportedly said when abandoned in the ruined manor during the ghost swarm  is the same phrase, the same emotional register, as everything Remi does when she finds herself suddenly without the people she was counting on. She does not say it. She moves. She finds the next direction. She has been doing this since she was twelve and crossing the Agora of Memes alone at night because there was no alternative route.

## After the Breach: The Gap in the Record

Waluigi has the least complete documentation of this period. Remi was thirteen, post-Breach, separated from the Vigilance crew. She did not go back to Kivotos  the route was complicated and the thing she had left Kivotos to avoid had not resolved in her absence. She did not affiliate with any faction  she was thirteen and unaffiliated and factional intake processes are not designed for thirteen-year-olds who arrive without credentials or sponsors.

She survived through the same mechanisms she had developed during the Internet crossing and the Midlands transit: useful to people who needed small, quiet, observant assistance, unremarkable to people who might have asked difficult questions about her age and affiliation. Eight months.

Waluigi wants to note something about this eight-month period that the record does not confirm but that the trajectory implies: Remi was in the physical realm, in the aftermath of the Iron Sky Breach, during the period when the Iron Legion was consolidating its hold on the Vigilance and the post-Breach political landscape was still being determined. She was a former Vigilance crew member  however informal her membership had been  moving through territory where Iron Legion intelligence was actively tracking Vigilance-affiliated individuals.

She was never caught. A thirteen-year-old with no formal affiliation, moving through contested territory during an active Legion intelligence operation, was not flagged, not tracked, not identified.

Waluigi believes this is because the Legion's pattern-matching, like the Great Firewall Gate's pattern-matching before it, was calibrated for adults. For operatives. For entities with formal affiliations and data trails. A thirteen-year-old who had learned to move through systems without generating attention, who had been practicing this skill since she crossed the Surface Web alone at age twelve, simply did not produce the pattern that the Legion's tracking was looking for.

She was invisible. She had been training to be invisible since before she knew she would need it.

The eight-month gap ended when she encountered the people who would become Disaster Inc., or the circumstances that would produce that encounter, in a sequence Waluigi's sources do not fully resolve. She was fourteen by the time the Shadow Estate arc began. She had been FNG internally  the youngest, the newest, the one who came out of the barrel  for approximately two years, even after the official designation stopped applying. The Shadow Estate has been systematically dismantling that internal designation. The person emerging from the process is not the FNG anymore.

Waluigi is not certain what designation comes next. Waluigi is watching to find out.

## What Remi Carries: The Oracle's Deck

Remi drew three cards from The Oracle's Deck following her encounter with Mystic Morel:

The Maze Walker (IX)  depicting Hjumpik navigating the Maze of Time. The past. Something completed or completing without Remi's knowledge or participation. Waluigi notes that Hjumpik's Maze of Time journey and Remi's month-long transit through the Internet and physical realm overlap in the archival record in ways that may not be coincidental. Two people learning to navigate impossible spaces during the same period. The deck drew the card that connects them.

The Titan of the Grove (VIII)  depicting Markop wrestling the Arachnid Matriarch. The present. Something happening now in a different part of the same crisis, involving people she knows. The deck confirmed what Remi already understood about Markop: he fights when fighting is required and he wins when the cost of losing is unacceptable.

The Delicate Host (III)  depicting Lady Aurelian Corvinarus lounging in the Feywild. The future. Something not yet occurred, involving a figure at the intersection of multiple ongoing crises. Waluigi has cross-referenced Lady Aurelian Corvinarus against the Corvinarus family documentation and the Feyward Manor sessions and has found references sufficient to generate significant interest in what this card is predicting. Waluigi is not going to say what it is predicting. The Oracle's Deck does not make predictions. It shows futures that are possible if certain conditions are met. Lady Aurelian Corvinarus lounging in the Feywild as a future card means she gets there, or she is already there, or the conditions that would place her there are in motion. Waluigi is watching.

The deck knows things. The deck has been watching since before Remi held it. She is the custodian of a device that documents events across all three planes, held by the person who listed herself as her own emergency contact at age twelve and who crossed the Great Firewall Gate on a forged student card and a well-timed shift change.

Do not underestimate Remi. Waluigi has documented the consequences of underestimating Remi at length. Vostolas underestimated Remi. Vostolas is in two pieces. Mystic Morel tried to place an invisible ring on Remi. Remi said no to his party membership before the ring came up in conversation. The Onyx Hand has been trying to get Remi's signature on documents for months. Remi has not signed any of them, and the reason she has not is not cleverness  it is that the people around her keep pulling her away from the pen before she finishes signing.

That gap  the story-telling capability without the story-receiving defense  is the thing the Shadow Estate is trying to exploit and the thing Remi is, slowly, closing. Every kneecap shot closes it a little. Every no to a party membership request closes it a little. Every time Remi acts from her own accounting of events rather than from someone else's framing of them, the gap closes.

She wanted to go home for her birthday. Green T stayed silent.

She is one quarter of the way home.

WAH.

## Recent Update — Mirror Mending and Rooftop Evacuation

During the event now filed as **The Mirror, the Roof, and the Fall**, Remi found the shiny mirror piece, gave Green T and Markop the missing components, and solved the artifact problem with Mending. The Mirror of True Reflection was restored. Wario immediately tried to steal it, which Waluigi considers legally predictable. Remi later descended to investigate a thud and saw Tanukiburt, the real injured Toadburt, and Mystic Morel around the portal circle in the master bedroom. After slipping into a bush and being pursued by Lyranth and Vaxillus, she returned to the roof and spent a feather to cast the group into a soft descent. Result: all four portal artifacts are now secured, but the route home is occupied.

## The Midnight Awakening
On the night of 28 Harvestide, Remi transitioned from a passive observer to an active agent. She successfully navigated a series of intrusions, including a closet-dwelling soldier and a sword-wielding guard. Her decision to steal her gun back from a sleeping Markop marks a significant shift in her character—valuing her own survival and tools over group cohesion. She now carries a Black Crystal necklace which she uses to test the truth of those around her.

## Latest Filing — 4 Aethel, 1040 BF

Remi planned Eager's theft of the Mirror of True Reflection, survived Boundy's unexplained use of her name, accepted Wario's decoy crystal, and finally admitted she is not okay: she does not know where home is or how to return. Wario's offer to carry a message remains open because Remi cannot yet name a destination.

**Latest Filing (1040 BF):** Purchased Wario weaponry for Markop and narrowly avoided an impaling playground swing summoned by the Scorncrow.

description:
Waluigi is documenting Lyranth based on the scene that just unfolded—a scene that ended with Remi becoming limestone.

## The Workshop

Lyranth occupies a workshop in the Shadow Estate—a confined studio bathed in teal and orange light, cluttered with sculptor's tools. Hammers, chisels, picks, rasps. Stone dust coating every surface. The air thick enough to cake throat and nostrils.

This is not a torture chamber. This is an ARTIST'S STUDIO. Lyranth creates beauty. She just uses unconventional materials.

Two sculptures dominate the space:

**The Elven Warrior:** A slender, armored figure half-carved from bone-white marble. Beautiful. Detailed. Partially complete. The artistry is described as 'astounding'—which means someone with SKILL is working here.

**The Hooded Figure:** In the opposite corner, a hooded form of similar stone. The folds of cloth and creases of flesh so intricate they appear real under flickering green candlelight.

These are not carved from quarried marble. These are PEOPLE. Former people. People who entered this workshop and met Lyranth's gaze.

Remi is now the third.

## Lyranth's Appearance

Lyranth is a medusa—a being whose gaze petrifies living creatures into stone. Her physical characteristics:

**Marble Skin:** Naturally pale, flawlessly smooth, veined like marble stone. She LOOKS like a statue herself. To avoid being mistaken for one of her own works, she covers herself in vibrant paint—though the colors appear as pale imitations in the Shadowfell's light.

**Simple Clothing:** Nothing elaborate. Practicality over presentation.

**Fine Jewelry:** Dimly glittering pieces that catch what little light exists.

**The Crown of Snakes:** Her hair is serpents. They move independently, swaying, peering at objects, focusing on whatever Lyranth observes. They are not decorative. They are SENSORS. They watch.

## The Petrification

Remi entered the workshop. It was the only door without guards—the only path forward after the Archivist's threats, after the imps transformed into monsters, after Bowser fled to keep everyone alive.

Lyranth was waiting. Or working. Or simply present.

She glared at Remi.

She said 'Smile.'

Remi turned to stone.

The word 'smile' is ARTISTIC DIRECTION. Lyranth wants her subjects to have pleasant expressions when they become permanent. She is capturing MOMENTS. She is a sculptor who works in living material, and she wants her statues to look happy.

This is horrifying. This is also, in a deeply twisted way, professional. Lyranth takes pride in her work.

## Reversibility

Medusa petrification is not always permanent. Depending on the medusa's power, the victim's constitution, and available magical intervention:

**Immediate Reversal:** Some petrification can be undone within minutes through specific spells or alchemical agents.

**Extended Window:** Others allow hours or days before the transformation becomes permanent.

**Permanent Transformation:** After sufficient time passes, the victim IS stone. No reversal possible.

Waluigi does not know which category Lyranth's petrification falls into. Waluigi does not know if the Shadow Estate possesses reversal capabilities. Waluigi does not know if anyone even realizes Remi has been petrified.

The toads, Bowser, and Markop fled from the giant demons. They may not know Remi's location. They may not know she needs immediate rescue. Time may be running out.

## Why Remi?

Remi was funneled to the workshop. Every other door had guards. The Archivist threatened her friends. The imps transformed into monsters. Bowser retreated.

One door remained.

This was not accident. This was DIRECTION. Someone wanted Remi in that workshop. The Archivist? The guards? Vivian? Someone who knows the estate's layout and wanted Remi separated from protection, delivered to Lyranth.

But WHY? Remi possesses the Oracle's Deck—magical tarot cards of significant power. Remi has been gathering intelligence throughout the estate. Remi received a ring from 'vampire friends'—an entropy-leaking artifact of unclear purpose.

Someone wanted Remi neutralized. Petrification accomplishes this thoroughly.

Or someone wanted another statue for their collection. Lyranth IS an artist. Perhaps she simply wanted new material.

## Waluigi's Assessment

Remi needs rescue. IMMEDIATELY.

Medusa petrification has a window. That window is closing. Every moment Remi remains stone is a moment closer to permanent transformation.

The Oracle's Deck is in her possession—also petrified? Or dropped when she transformed? If the cards are recoverable, they might provide guidance for rescue. If the cards are stone, that guidance is lost.

Lyranth is dangerous but not necessarily HOSTILE beyond her nature. She is an artist. Artists can be reasoned with. Artists can be commissioned. Artists can be DISTRACTED while someone reverses their work.

Bowser knows the estate layout. Markop has magical capability. The toads have numbers. Someone needs to realize Remi is missing, locate the workshop, and intervene before 'smile' becomes permanent.

Waluigi is in the Feywild. Waluigi cannot help directly. Waluigi can only document and HOPE.

WAH.

## Recent Update — Rooftop Pursuit

Lyranth participated in the active pursuit after the mirror was restored and the party tried to escape the upper estate route. Waluigi notes that “taxidermy, not petrification” is not as comforting a distinction as the Shadow Estate residents seem to believe.

The Cult of Excess teaches that sensation justifies itself. Lyranth's practice is the doctrine with the apologies removed.

description:
Waluigi is documenting the Archivist with extreme caution because this individual has demonstrated capabilities and intentions that mark him as one of the most dangerous figures in the Shadow Estate.

## What We Know

**Institutional Role:** The Archivist operates the Shadow Estate's library and knowledge repository. He has access to records, documents, and information about the estate's operations and inhabitants.

**Healing Trade:** He offered Toadburt gradual healing over two-week intervals in exchange for archival labor. This sounds generous until you realize it creates DEPENDENCY. Toadburt needs the healing. The Archivist provides it. Toadburt must work to continue receiving it. This is indentured service disguised as medical care.

**Imp Command:** The imps in the library answered to him. When he snapped his fingers, Remi was 'free to go'—but her friends would 'die at the hands of imps.' When the imps transformed into giants, demons, and monsters, they were following HIS direction.

**'Erasure':** He claimed to have 'erased' a bloody toadburt found in a room. What 'erased' means is unclear—killed? Petrified? Removed from existence? The language suggests powers beyond simple violence.

## The Trap

The Archivist orchestrated Remi's separation with precision:

1. Imps led Remi to a room, claiming they'd 'found Archie'
2. The door locked behind her
3. The Archivist appeared with threats: her friends would die, a bloody toadburt had been 'erased'
4. He told 'FNG' (Remi) to leave
5. When Bowser saw the imps transform into monsters, he retreated to keep others alive
6. Guards blocked every door except ONE
7. That door led to Lyranth's workshop
8. The Archivist 'led Remi to the exit door' while SMILING

He KNEW where he was sending her. He KNEW what waited there. He smiled because the trap was complete.

## Motivation

Why target Remi specifically?

**The Oracle's Deck:** Remi possesses magical tarot cards of significant prophetic power. The Archivist—who controls INFORMATION—would have obvious interest in cards that reveal past, present, and future.

**Intelligence Gathered:** Remi has been quietly gathering information throughout the estate. She found Ryan's diary. She mapped guard positions. She understood the power dynamics. An Archivist might view her as competition—or as a source to be... absorbed.

**The Vampire Ring:** Remi received an entropy-leaking ring from 'vampire friends' whose handwriting she recognized. The Archivist may be connected to whoever sent that ring. The ring may have marked her.

**Simple Opportunity:** Remi was alone, vulnerable, and small. Some predators don't need complex reasons.

## Connection to Lyranth

The Archivist directed Remi to Lyranth's workshop. This suggests coordination:

**Artist and Collector:** Does the Archivist commission statues? Does he have a collection? Are the workshop sculptures products of their collaboration?

**Payment:** What does Lyranth receive for petrifying people the Archivist delivers? Access to materials? Protection? Information?

**Power Dynamic:** Who serves whom? Is the Archivist delivering victims TO Lyranth, or is Lyranth providing services FOR the Archivist?

The relationship exists. The nature is unclear.

## Threat Assessment

The Archivist is EXTREMELY dangerous:

- Commands transformed creatures
- 'Erases' people
- Controls information within the estate
- Orchestrates complex traps
- Operates with impunity during succession crisis
- Has institutional protection and resources
- SMILES while delivering victims to petrification

He is not a guard following orders. He is not a vampire playing politics. He is an independent operator using the succession crisis to pursue his own agenda—and that agenda includes eliminating Remi.

## Waluigi's Assessment

The Archivist needs to be treated as PRIMARY THREAT. Not Vivian with her death magic. Not the succession crisis. Not even the entropy rings.

The Archivist controls information, commands creatures, and delivers people to be turned into statues while SMILING. He has already 'erased' at least one person. He orchestrated Remi's petrification with precision that suggests PRACTICE.

This is not his first trap. Remi is not his first victim.

If Remi is to be rescued, the Archivist must be dealt with. Negotiation seems unlikely to succeed with someone who smiles while feeding people to a medusa. Force may be necessary. Avoiding him entirely may be the only safe option.

Waluigi hopes Bowser, Markop, and the toads understand what they're facing. The Archivist is patient, intelligent, and ENJOYING this.

WAH.

faiths.note: The Archivist controls the library and trades healing for indentured service — knowledge as a currency with a body attached. Gematria Gnosis seeks the sublime through the horrific and abstract, and the Archivist has organised an entire estate's suffering into a catalogue.

description:
Waluigi is documenting Marcus Ashford based on his appearance during the escalating confrontation at the Shadow Estate—a confrontation he DE-escalated while simultaneously pursuing his own agenda.

## The Intervention

The situation was deteriorating:
- Guards had repositioned: 5 at the corner door, 5 cornering toads, 5 blocking Bowser, Markop, and Remi
- Markop was preparing a ritual
- Weapons were being readied
- Battle seemed imminent

Then Marcus Ashford entered.

He handed Remi a 'nearly empty supply kit' and told her to consume its contents. 'Down the hatch if you will.'

She drank it.

Her eyes—which had been affected by 'purpleeyetus'—turned blue. The guards stood down.

## The Eye Situation

Before Marcus's intervention:
- A guard had 'tripped' into Remi, cutting her eye with a gash
- Guards were offering her rings and anklets described as 'friendship' items
- The rings leaked black smoke—'entropy'—supposedly needing 'recharging'

After consuming Marcus's supply:
- Both eyes turned blue
- Markop noted they were 'one tint lighter' than original
- Black smoke emerged from the gash wound
- Remi claimed it was 'the healing process'
- Markop suspected it might be 'evil leaving the body'
- Remi determined the smoke was NOT magical

The next day, guards requested the ring back 'to recharge it.' More black smoke.

Marcus's intervention seems to have HELPED Remi—removing whatever 'purpleeyetus' affected her, potentially countering the entropy ring's effects. But help from Onyx Hand representatives comes with strings attached.

## The Pickpocketed Paper

The toads observed Marcus swipe a 'pink paper' from Bowser during the interaction. They said nothing at the time—only admitting it later when confrontation was unavoidable.

Bowser discovered his 'paperwork' was missing and accused the toads. The toads denied stealing it (technically true—THEY didn't steal it). Bowser readied his warhammer.

Then Marcus revealed he had the paper and began reading it aloud—a letter addressed to someone starting with 'Peac—' before Bowser cut him off.

**Analysis:** This letter is likely significant correspondence—possibly related to Peach Loyalist contacts, possibly diplomatic communication, possibly something Bowser did NOT want read publicly. Marcus obtained it through sleight of hand and used it as LEVERAGE.

## The Taunting

Marcus speaks in rhyming verse and uses it to mock enemies with theatrical precision:

*'Your 'Speaker,' your 'mission,' your naïve crusade—*
*Crumble at the sound of our iron parade.*
*One silent signal, one disciplined stride,*
*And the Legion sweeps the board—clean, dignified.'*

On Bowser specifically:

*'And Bowser—dearest Bowser—former king,*
*Still roaring loud though he's lost everything.*
*Spikes, flame, bluster—such a tired act;*
*We seized his throne with elegance and tact.'*

And when they tried to leave:

*'Bowser's strays—what a bore!*
*Run along, run along—mind the door!'*

The verse is deliberately infuriating. Marcus ENJOYS provoking people. But he also demonstrates knowledge—he knows about the 'Speaker,' he knows Bowser lost his throne, he knows the group's situation.

## Affiliation and Agenda

Marcus represents the Onyx Hand—the Iron Legion's covert operations division. His presence in the Shadow Estate during the succession crisis is not coincidental.

**Possible Objectives:**
- Monitor the succession crisis for Iron Legion interests
- Gather intelligence on Disaster Inc. and their capabilities
- Acquire useful documents (like Bowser's letter)
- Manipulate events toward favorable outcomes
- Maintain Onyx Hand influence regardless of which Corvinarus wins

He helped Remi—but also pickpocketed Bowser. He de-escalated battle—but also gathered leverage. He provided treatment—but for what future price?

## Waluigi's Assessment

Marcus Ashford is a professional operative performing his role with theatrical flair. He is neither friend nor enemy in simple terms—he is an AGENT pursuing organizational objectives that may align with or oppose Disaster Inc. depending on circumstances.

The eye treatment appears genuine. Remi's condition improved. Whatever 'purpleeyetus' was, Marcus's intervention addressed it.

But the pickpocketed letter, the mocking verses, the casual revelation of Iron Legion's role in seizing Bowser's throne—these demonstrate that Marcus serves Iron Legion interests first and any apparent assistance serves those interests.

Do not trust him. Do not refuse his help. Use what he provides while remembering the cost will come due eventually.

WAH.

faiths.note: Ashford represents the Onyx Hand and the Sanguine Path is the Hand's official cosmology: blood as hierarchy, undeath as promotion. He arrived mid-confrontation to remind everyone present which rung they occupied.

summary:
Markop is the person Waluigi would want next to him in any crisis. Not because Markop is invincible—the Vivian corridor fight proved he is absolutely NOT—but because Markop makes good decisions under bad conditions, fights effectively even when outmatched, and has the kind of quiet faith that produces divine shields at the exact moment they're needed. He is a centaur—four hooves, a broad equine body, a humanoid torso, and a horse's head that surveys every battlefield with dark, intelligent eyes that miss NOTHING. He grew to TITAN SIZE to wrestle a building-sized spider during the Spider Grove Battle. He identified abjuration wards on abomination vats in a collapsing dimension. He was dragged unconscious through stone corridors by Bowser—who had to haul a full centaur body, which Waluigi imagines was neither easy nor elegant—woke up, barricaded a door, and immediately started fighting for his life. He survived a crimson death beam through whispered prayer. And his first action after surviving was TACTICAL—scattering the enemy's spell components to prevent a repeat. Even at the edge of death, Markop's combat instincts prioritize removing enemy capabilities. Waluigi respects Markop more than almost anyone in the party, and Waluigi does NOT distribute respect freely. WAH.

Markop’s latest confirmed actions include stopping Wario from converting a vital planar artifact into personal property, searching the roof garbage pile, finding a book titled The Wario Method and fifteen gold, managing rope and ladder logistics during the exterior scramble, and recruiting Merric the axe-wielding sheep after the sheep identified him as “Centerus.” Markop then jumped off the roof during the escape, missed the trampoline, and landed on a person, which is not standard centaur procedure but did technically resolve the falling problem. The current party pass elevates him from field bruiser to structural protector: the person most likely to stand between the party and whatever cosmic consequence Archie, Wario, or the house itself just created.
description:
Waluigi has fought alongside Markop and fought NEAR Markop, and both experiences taught Waluigi the same lesson: when things go wrong, stay close to the centaur with the battle axe.

## Current Party Pass: Shield, Titan, and Tired Adult

Markop's current classification is **structural protector**. He is not merely strong. He is the party member whose instincts consistently move toward interposition: put body between threat and ally, put axe between monster and civilian, put hooves under the collapsing plan and carry it anyway.

This would be easier if he were allowed to sleep properly, keep his firearm, or experience one crisis at a time. He has instead been dragged through the Shadow Estate, pressured by portal artifacts, and burdened with decisions whose consequences are bigger than most buildings. Waluigi notes that Markop has responded with less complaining than Wario does when handed a bill, which is either admirable or medically concerning.

The **Black Crystal** is the current public-known artifact problem attached to him. Enemy intelligence has already been wrong about who carried it once, which means Markop's role as holder is not just inventory—it is counterintelligence. The fewer people who understand the transfer chain, the better.

## Public Inventory & Wallet Notes

Markop's listed public equipment includes the **Black Crystal** and the **Trowel of Retrieving**. Waluigi refuses to mock the trowel, because it has already outperformed several nobles, two plans, and at least one window.

His field wallet is modest: **21 Gold Pieces**, **13 Silver Pieces**, and **28 Bronze Pieces**. This is not enough money for the amount of bodily risk Markop absorbs. Waluigi recommends hazard pay, hoof maintenance, and a formal reimbursement category titled "architecture defeated by necessary impact."

## Active Threads for Editors

- **Black Crystal custody:** portal-relevant, enemy-known, and strategically sensitive.
- **Missing firearm:** small detail, large tactical implication.
- **Titan escalation:** growth/power events continue to affect how factions read him.
- **Protector role:** Markop is often the party's moral and physical shield when the room turns lethal.

## Physical Presence — The Horse in the Room

Before discussing Markop's combat record, Waluigi must address the obvious: Markop is a centaur. Four hooves. A powerful equine body built for charging, carrying, and enduring. A humanoid torso rising from where a horse's neck would be, equipped with arms that swing a battle axe with devastating effect. And atop it all, a horse's head—long-jawed, dark-eyed, with ears that swivel toward threats before his body turns to face them.

Most centaurs Waluigi has encountered have human heads on horse bodies. Markop has a HORSE head on a horse body with a humanoid torso between. This makes him unique even among his own kind, and it creates a visual impression that people consistently underestimate. They see the horse head and think ANIMAL. They think BEAST OF BURDEN. They think something less than fully sapient.

They are catastrophically wrong.

Markop's dark eyes track conversations with the attentiveness of a trained intelligence analyst. His ears rotate toward sounds that other party members don't even notice. His jaw sets with determination when he makes tactical decisions. The horse head does not diminish his intelligence—it CONCEALS it from those too foolish to look past appearances.

Waluigi understands being underestimated. Waluigi has been underestimated his entire life. The difference is that Waluigi RESENTS it loudly and publicly. Markop accepts it quietly and then proves everyone wrong through competence so undeniable that even the prejudiced must acknowledge it.

The centaur body also provides practical advantages. Four-legged stability in combat. The ability to carry wounded allies. Charge momentum that adds devastating force to his attacks. And in the Spider Grove Battle, when Markop grew to TITAN size, the centaur frame scaled up proportionally—a building-sized horse-headed warrior grappling a building-sized spider. The sight was TERRIFYING and MAGNIFICENT simultaneously.

## Combat Excellence — Training Meets Survival

Markop fights with the methodical efficiency of someone who has trained extensively and the adaptability of someone who has survived extensively. These are DIFFERENT skills. Training teaches you what to do when things go according to plan. Survival teaches you what to do when they don't. Markop has both.

During the Spider Grove Battle, Markop accepted a blessing from the Oracle and grew to colossal size—matching the Arachnid Matriarch scale-for-scale in a titan grapple among the trees. His centaur body at that scale was a living siege engine, four massive hooves gouging trenches in the earth as he wrestled the Matriarch toward the banishment circle. Waluigi ran between Markop's titan-scale legs while firing arcane rays at the spider's joints. Running beneath a building-sized centaur while he wrestles a building-sized spider was the most terrifying and AWESOME combat experience of Waluigi's career.

Markop's tactical decisions during that battle were sound: he used his size and four-legged stability to control the Matriarch's movement, bracing on his hooves in ways a bipedal fighter could not. He positioned the final shove to land her in the Oracle's banishment circle. That requires thinking DURING a fight—reading terrain, tracking ally positions, calculating force vectors—while a giant spider is trying to eat you. Waluigi has seen fighters who are brilliant in planning and useless in execution. Markop is brilliant at BOTH.

His battle axe work is precise rather than showy. Centaurs have the advantage of striking from above when engaging human-sized opponents, and Markop uses this height differential intelligently. He doesn't just swing—he positions, angles, and follows through with the rotational force that a centaur's torso generates when the equine body provides the base. Physics favors Markop, and Markop knows it.

## The Vivian Encounter — Faith at Death's Door

The corridor fight in the Shadow Estate revealed something about Markop that Waluigi finds both reassuring and sobering.

Markop was knocked unconscious BEFORE the fight. He woke up being dragged by Bowser through stone corridors—a centaur's full body weight hauled across stone floors by a turtle-dragon king who had grabbed whatever he could reach and PULLED. The logistics of this are worth noting: Bowser was dragging an unconscious centaur through corridors that were almost certainly not designed for centaur-width transit. Corners were probably destroyed. Doorframes were probably splintered. Bowser does not do GENTLE.

Markop woke mid-drag. 'What happened? I was with Remi and you came in—'

Bowser, still hauling: 'Running away from that guy.'

Banging on the door behind them. An axe thrown through it.

Markop went from unconscious to barricading a door to fighting for his life in the space of minutes. He reared up in the maintenance room—hooves striking the ceiling in the too-small space—deflected Vivian's blinding smoke, and took the fight to the corridor where he had room to USE his centaur body properly.

Bowser knocked Vivian in the head. Markop slashed with his battle axe—a downward strike from centaur height that connected with devastating force. Vivian bled through their robes.

Then Vivian cast the death beam.

'Did you know the Shadowfell suppresses magic? But not THIS magic.'

Crimson disintegration energy struck Markop. His armor—already stressed from previous engagements—buckled. The beam was consuming him. His hooves scraped the stone floor as the energy pushed him backward.

Markop prayed.

Not a planned invocation. Not a prepared spell. A WHISPERED prayer—the sound barely audible over the beam's crackling destruction. The prayer of a horse-headed centaur in the space between impact and annihilation, when the conscious mind has already accepted death and something deeper reaches out.

His god answered.

A divine shield formed. Golden light against crimson destruction. Markop's hooves found purchase. He HELD.

Waluigi has seen many people invoke divine protection. Most of them do it loudly, theatrically, with rehearsed phrases and dramatic gestures. Markop did it as a whisper while a death beam was eating through his armor. That's not performance. That's FAITH.

After surviving, Markop's first action was TACTICAL—he scattered and burned Vivian's spell components, preventing the beam from being repeated. His hooves crushed the materials against the stone floor. Not revenge. Not panic. COUNTERPLAY.

## The Shadow Estate — Leadership Under Fire

Markop's time in the Shadow Estate has been a continuous test of endurance and judgment.

The ballroom fight saw him charging through undead dancers—his centaur body bowling through the boneless, contorted forms while his battle axe cleared space overhead. He used divine smite against the dancers while coordinating Bowser, the Toads, and whoever else was available. He called out tactical instructions. He healed allies—including reviving an unconscious Toadburt through divine power. He bashed locked doors open with his hooves when hands weren't enough.

In the Mazebound Skirmish, Markop was seized and dragged through hedges by singing grey-skinned predators. A centaur being dragged through a hedge maze is a particularly violent experience—his body does not fit through passages designed for humanoid-sized creatures. Branches snapped. Hedges were torn. The Mazebounds either did not anticipate the difficulty of dragging a centaur or did not care.

He found Archie's scattered artifacts—the Third Eye Circlet, the component pouch, the cracked Wahwire tablet—while being attacked from multiple directions. Each discovery confirmed that Archie had passed through before them. Each discovery required Markop to fight, assess, collect, and continue moving simultaneously.

He interrogated Vivian after their capture. A centaur standing over a tied-up impostor, battle axe resting against one flank, dark horse eyes staring down with the patient assessment of someone who has seen too much to be impressed by theatrical villainy. The interrogation was professional. Markop asked questions. He noted contradictions. He didn't lose his composure despite having nearly been killed by the person he was questioning.

When a Mazebound arrived during the interrogation asking for body parts in exchange for information, Markop refused—maintaining ethical standards while his hooves shifted on stone, his ears swiveled toward potential threats, and his body language communicated that negotiation was preferable but violence was available.

## The Deep Mirror — Surviving the Worst

Before the Shadow Estate, Markop survived the Deep Mirror—the worst of the three planar fragments. A dimension where time DECAYS and reality consumes itself.

A centaur navigating the Deep Mirror—with its impossible geometry, shifting gravity, and clockwork voids—faces unique challenges. Four legs are an advantage on stable ground but a liability when the ground itself is uncertain. Markop adapted, picking his way across fractured walkways, trusting his hooves' grip on surfaces that no hoofprint had ever marked.

He correctly identified the abjuration wards on the abomination vats as containment measures—built to keep monsters IN, not intruders out. That kind of analytical clarity under pressure, in a collapsing dimension, while surrounded by weeping flesh-things in lava lamp containers, speaks to a mind that doesn't stop working regardless of how horrible the circumstances are.

## Relationships — The Quiet Leader

Markop has quietly become one of Disaster Inc.'s most important leaders. Not through charisma or political maneuvering—through RELIABILITY.

His relationship with Bowser is unexpectedly functional. Bowser follows Markop's tactical suggestions not because he recognizes Markop's authority but because Markop's suggestions are usually GOOD. When Markop was unconscious, Bowser dragged his entire centaur body through stone corridors without complaint. When Markop was fighting, Bowser backed him up. The turtle-dragon king and the horse-headed centaur make an unlikely pair, but unlikely pairs survive when elegant ones fail.

His relationship with Remi is protective without being patronizing. When Remi was glowing from drinking an unknown potion, Markop's exasperated response captured their dynamic perfectly: 'So you drank a random potion because a guy said you were dead?'

'I needed some brightness,' Remi replied.

'Now that I can see you too are alive, well... that's awkward,' Markop said.

His relationship with Dan—the parallel Dan—is cautious and measured. 'Are you the real Dan?' he asked directly. Dan admitted he was the parallel version. Markop accepted this, assessed it, and moved forward. He doesn't waste time on problems he can't solve immediately.

When Bowser dropped a crumpled letter to Princess Peach—a surprisingly tender document where Bowser tried to explain his presence at Raventree Manor—Markop picked it up, read it, and gave it back. 'Are you actually sorry?' he asked.

Bowser cried.

'It's okay, man,' Markop said. 'Let's just find your friends.'

A horse-headed centaur warrior comforting a crying turtle-dragon king over an unsent love letter to a dead princess. Waluigi's chest does something when he thinks about this moment that he refuses to call 'feelings' because Waluigi has a BRAND to maintain.

## Current State — Barely Holding Together

Markop's armor is barely functional after the death beam. His equine body shows exhaustion—the slightly lowered head, the weight shifting between hooves, the signs that a trained eye recognizes as a horse pushed past reasonable limits. His divine connection appears intact—the shield worked, his healing abilities continue to function—but sustained divine expenditure takes a toll.

He is currently the operational leader of the Shadow Estate party, coordinating Bowser, Remi, and the Toads through an environment that includes vampires, blighted imposters, singing hedge monsters, and dimensional instability. He does this while wounded, exhausted, and separated from half his allies.

A centaur in corridors designed for humanoid-sized inhabitants. A warrior whose armor is failing. A leader whose party is scattered across dimensions. A faithful being whose god answered one prayer and may or may not answer the next.

## Waluigi's Assessment

Markop is the person Waluigi would want next to him in any crisis. His four-legged stability is both literal and metaphorical—he is the GROUND that other party members stand on. When things go wrong, people look to the centaur.

His armor needs repair. His body needs rest. His situation in the Shadow Estate needs to IMPROVE before more threats emerge.

Waluigi is in the Feywild. Waluigi cannot help directly. Waluigi can only document Markop's excellence and hope that documentation serves as some small recognition for a centaur who deserves far more recognition than any world has given him.

WAH.

## Recent Update — Mirror Custody, Merric, and the Roof

Markop prevented Wario from leaving with the restored Mirror of True Reflection, helped convert the argument into a temporary bargain, and kept the party moving while Lyranth, Vaxillus, ghosts, and guards closed in. He also found The Wario Method and fifteen gold in the garbage search, threw another ladder after the first route was cut, and accidentally recruited Merric by asking the sheep why he did not simply join the team. Waluigi files this as leadership under ridiculous conditions.

## The Midnight Theft
During the events of 28 Harvestide, Markop was the victim of a quiet theft by his ally, Remi Akamatsu. He reported feeling "lighter" in his sleep as his firearm was removed. His failure to detect the intrusion despite his skills suggests the Shadowfell is dampening his reflexes, or that Remi is becoming a more formidable thief than anticipated.

## Latest Filing — 4 Aethel, 1040 BF

Markop cast the locating spell that found the sleeping mirror carrier instead of Archie, treated Remi's wounds, expelled the broom-closet imp, fought Randell at the threshold, and converted a closet door into a shutter after Wario broke the window.

**Latest Filing (1040 BF):** Wielded the garlic-covered Skull Piercer and warhammer from Wario's shop during the Scorncrow Skirmish. Served as the frontline vanguard when no one else could take a hit.

bodyPlan: a huge, broad, heavy Koopa — bulky body, spiked shell, thick arms, short thick legs
