name: Merric
title: The Axe-Wielding Sheep Who Joined the Team Because Why Not
status: Active — recruited during the Shadow Estate rooftop escape after calling Markop “Centerus”
affiliation: Shadow Estate escape party / new Disaster Inc.-linked ally
summary: Merric is an axe-wielding sheep encountered during the Shadow Estate sequence. He behaved as if he was already part of the team, then failed Markop’s identity check by calling him “Centerus,” then accepted the correction not by apologizing but by joining the team for real. Waluigi respects this recruitment method because it is fast, confusing, and paperwork-light.
description:
Merric entered the record during the Shadow Estate upper-floor chaos as a sheep with an axe and enough confidence to critique Markop's violence. During the rooftop escape sequence, the party finally asked who he actually was. Merric's answer pattern established two facts: he did not know Markop's name, and he was willing to become part of the team anyway.

## The Sheep With An Axe

The Shadow Estate has produced ghosts, vampires, a medusa, a beastmaster, singing servants, and a shapeshifter at the exit, so an armed, opinionated, self-appointed teammate in the shape of a sheep is, by local standards, almost reasonable. Merric arrived behaving as though he had always been part of Disaster Inc., offered live commentary on Markop's fighting technique, and generally conducted himself with the serene confidence of someone who has never once doubted his own belonging.

## The Centerus Incident

The party eventually attempted to verify this newcomer. Markop asked Merric what his name was. Merric answered "Centerus"—which was wrong, being neither his name nor Markop's. Markop, rather than pressing the point, asked why Merric did not simply join their team instead. Merric thought about it and said sure, why not. Waluigi files this as the cleanest recruitment in Disaster Inc. history: no oath, no interview, no paperwork, just a sheep agreeing to a stranger's suggestion mid-crisis.

## A Worrying Kind Of Simple

Waluigi respects Merric's recruitment method because it is fast, confusing, and paperwork-light—all qualities Waluigi values in principle. He remains wary in practice, because "we acquired a heavily armed ally who does not know our names and joined on a whim during a rooftop escape" is the sort of sentence that reads as convenient right up until it does not. For now, Merric wields his axe on the correct side of the fight, which is all Waluigi asks of anyone.

title: The Toadburt-Shaped Problem at the Portal Circle
status: Active — discovered at the Shadow Estate portal circle with Mystic Morel and the injured real Toadburt
affiliation: Shadow Estate portal-circle hostiles / enemy wildcard
summary: Tanukiburt is the newest and least welcome answer to the Toadburt question: a Tanuki-shaped or Toadburt-shaped problem found at the master-bedroom portal circle alongside Mystic Morel and the injured real Toadburt. Waluigi does not yet know the full mechanics. Waluigi does know that if a person named Tanukiburt is standing next to the real Toadburt at the only exit, the correct response is screaming followed by tactical planning.
description:
Tanukiburt was confirmed during Remi's scouting after the Mirror of True Reflection was repaired. Looking into the master bedroom from outside, Remi saw Tanukiburt, the real injured Toadburt, and Mystic Morel gathered around the portal circle while the rug was being manipulated. This places Tanukiburt at the party's immediate route home and makes him a direct obstacle to activating the Midnight Fountain or using the portal safely.

## The Toadburt Question, Made Worse

For a while the Toadburt situation was a straightforward missing-person problem: the Iron Legion's coerced operative had slipped free of his entropy ring and gone to work for the Shadow Estate's Archivist in exchange for healing, and the party simply wanted to know where he had gone. Tanukiburt's appearance detonated that simplicity. Standing beside the real, injured Toadburt is a second Toadburt-shaped figure, which converts a location problem into an identity problem—and identity problems, Waluigi notes, cannot be solved with a tennis racket.

## Shapeshifter At The Door

Everything about Tanukiburt's staging is hostile. He is at the portal circle. He is beside Mystic Morel, the singing prophet-thief who opens planar doorways. He is between Disaster Inc. and the only known exit. Whether Tanukiburt is a Tanuki impersonator, a magical duplicate, or some other trickster construct is unresolved, but the placement is unambiguous: he is a guard on the last threshold.

## Current Threat Meaning

Tanukiburt's presence means the Toadburt situation is no longer just "where is Toadburt?" It is now "which Toadburt, why are there two, and how many of them are standing between the party and home?" A shapeshifter guarding the exit is the specific nightmare that turns every rescue into an interrogation. Waluigi hates riddles that stand in doorways.

name: Vaxillus the Beastmaster
title: The Taxidermy Enthusiast Remi Used as a Ladder
status: Active — pursuing the party with Lyranth after the mirror recovery; unwillingly used as Remi’s ladder
summary: Vaxillus the Beastmaster is a Shadow Estate pursuer whose current confirmed role includes waving from below, threatening the party with taxidermy-adjacent intentions, being used by Remi as a biological ladder, and then carrying Lyranth into the second story so the hunt could continue upward. Waluigi dislikes him but admits the ladder part was funny.
description:
Vaxillus entered the immediate Shadow Estate escape record as part of the exterior pursuit after Remi discovered the occupied portal circle. He and Lyranth did not appear to be trying to petrify the party. They appeared to prefer stuffing them into taxidermy, which Waluigi considers a distinction without comfort.

## A Different Kind Of Threat

The Shadow Estate is full of ways to die, and Vaxillus represents one of its more disturbing specialties. Where the medusa Lyranth turns victims to stone, Vaxillus's threat is taxidermy-adjacent—the promise of being preserved, posed, and displayed rather than merely killed. Waluigi has cataloged many hazards in this encyclopedia. "Will stuff you and mount you on a wall" ranks high on the list of fates a person should sprint away from.

## The Biological Ladder Incident

Vaxillus's confirmed contributions to the escape sequence include waving from below, threatening the party, and—memorably—being used by Remi as a living ladder. During the attempt to reach the roof, Remi climbed him like scaffolding, prompting a guard to yell, "HEY, BE CAREFUL WITH THAT THING." Waluigi believes this is the first known Estate safety warning ever issued on behalf of a hostile pursuer being climbed by a fourteen-year-old with an urgent schedule.

## Ally To The Hunt

After the climb, Vaxillus carried Lyranth into the second story so the pursuit could continue upward, cementing his role as a mobile piece of the Estate's hunting apparatus rather than a lone predator. Waluigi dislikes him on principle—he is, after all, trying to turn the party into decor—but concedes that the ladder part was genuinely funny, and that this encyclopedia would be poorer without the phrase "biological ladder incident" in it.

summary: Rattles is a skeleton recruited from a servant closet who wants to turn back time and regain his original flesh-and-bones body, not a replacement. He speaks with deeply skeleton-appropriate timing, joined the party during the Shadow Estate servant corridor sequence, and survived the rooftop escape by grabbing onto Remi during Feather Fall.
description:
Rattles first entered the record during the servant corridor investigation, where he was found with an antique frog and a goblet. He wanted his old body back specifically, which Waluigi finds unusually precise for a skeleton in a closet.

## A Very Specific Wish

Most reanimated skeletons, in Waluigi's experience, want either revenge, rest, or someone's soul. Rattles wants something oddly technical: to turn back time and regain his original flesh-and-bones body—not a replacement, not an upgrade, the exact one he had before. This precision suggests Rattles remembers being alive clearly enough to be picky about it, which makes him less a monster and more a person filing a very difficult complaint with the universe.

## Recruited From A Closet

Rattles joined the party during the Shadow Estate servant corridor sequence, arriving with an antique frog and a goblet like a man who had been interrupted mid-errand a very long time ago. He speaks with deeply skeleton-appropriate timing, which Waluigi will not define further except to say that the delivery lands. He fit into Disaster Inc. immediately, on the grounds that a group this chaotic barely notices one more improbable member.

## Recent Update — Feather Fall Escape

During The Mirror, the Roof, and the Fall, Rattles remained with the rooftop group while Lyranth, Vaxillus, ghosts, guards, and singing servants turned the upper estate into a death box. When the escape came, he grabbed onto Remi and descended safely under Feather Fall. Waluigi notes that "skeleton survives fall by holding onto a child with a magic feather" is legally a sentence but emotionally a problem, and files it under the growing list of things the Shadow Estate has made normal.

## Latest Filing — 4 Aethel, 1040 BF

Rattles stayed at Tymnas's cottage during the lockdown and used a piece of his own backbone to brace a window until Markop could set the proper lock.
